name: Kanhoji Jedhe
summary: Head of the Jedhe family, Deshmukh of the Kari region, and one of the earliest and most senior Maval chieftains to join Shivaji's rising. The Jedhe family's own chronicle, the Jedhe Shakavali, is among the earliest surviving Maratha historical records. Birth and death years not firmly attested; entered as approximate estimates.

relationships.note: One of the earliest and most senior Maval chieftains to join him; head of a family whose own chronicle (the Jedhe Shakavali) is a primary source for this period.

name: Firangoji Narsala
summary: Commanded the garrison at Chakan fort against the Mughal siege led by Shaista Khan's forces in 1660, holding out for about six weeks before the fort fell. Taken prisoner, he was reportedly offered a position in Mughal service in recognition of his defense but returned to Shivaji's service instead.

relationships.note: Held Chakan fort against Shaista Khan's siege for about six weeks in 1660.

journey.label: Defends Chakan fort
journey.summary: Commands the garrison at Chakan against the besieging Mughal army under Shaista Khan.

name: Annaji Datto
summary: Served as Sachiv, one of the eight ministers of Shivaji's Ashta Pradhan council, handling administrative and secretarial duties. After Shivaji's death in 1680 he was drawn into the succession dispute between Sambhaji and Rajaram's faction; Sambhaji had him executed in 1681 for alleged conspiracy.

relationships.note: Served as Sachiv, one of the eight ministers of his Ashta Pradhan council.
Executed in 1681 for alleged involvement in a conspiracy during the succession dispute after Shivaji's death.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

namesakes.name: Shivaji II of Kolhapur
namesakes.note: Grandson; son of Rajaram and Tarabai.

summary: Built a kingdom in the western Deccan out of Bijapur and Mughal territory and was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at the hill fort of Shivneri near Junnar.

journey.label: Settles on the Pune jagir
journey.summary: Jijabai and the young Shivaji settle on Shahaji’s estate at Pune after Shahaji enters Bijapur service.
journey.routeNote: The family’s movements during the wars of 1630–36 are poorly recorded.

journey.label: Takes Torna fort
journey.summary: Gains control of the Bijapur hill fort of Torna, the first of a chain of forts around Pune.
journey.routeNote: The year is traditional; some works give 1647.

journey.label: Meeting with Afzal Khan
journey.summary: Kills the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at a parley; the Bijapur army is routed.

journey.label: Escape from the siege of Panhala
journey.summary: Breaks out of the besieged fort of Panhala by night and reaches Vishalgad, covered by Baji Prabhu Deshpande's stand at Pavan Khind.

journey.label: Raid on Shaista Khan
journey.summary: Leads a night raid on the Mughal viceroy’s residence.

journey.label: Sack of Surat
journey.summary: Plunders the Mughal port for several days.
journey.routeNote: A fast cavalry march; the road taken is not recorded.

journey.label: Treaty with Jai Singh
journey.summary: Agrees to cede 23 forts and serve the empire.

journey.label: Court audience
journey.summary: Presented to Aurangzeb, protests his placing and is put under guard.
journey.routeNote: Left Rajgad in March 1666 and travelled north through Aurangabad and Burhanpur.

journey.label: Return after escape
journey.summary: Reaches his capital at Rajgad late in the year.
journey.routeNote: Later narratives describe a long eastern detour through Mathura, Allahabad, Varanasi and Golconda. No contemporary record of the route exists.

journey.label: Second raid on Surat
journey.summary: Raids Surat again in October while recovering the forts ceded in 1665.

journey.label: Coronation
journey.summary: Crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad.

journey.label: Southern campaign
journey.summary: Marches into the Karnatak, meets the Qutb Shah at Hyderabad on the way, and takes the fortress of Gingee.
journey.routeNote: The march passed through Hyderabad early in 1677.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Raigad on 3 April.

relationships.note: Bijapur general sent against him in 1659; killed at the parley on Pratapgad.
Mughal viceroy of the Deccan; Shivaji’s 1663 night raid on his Pune quarters cost him three fingers and a son.
Mughal commander who besieged Purandar in 1665 and forced the treaty ceding 23 forts; the two then met on cordial terms.
Childhood friend from Jijabai’s household and a trusted commander; died retaking Sinhagad for him in 1670.
His first Sarnaubat (commander-in-chief); captured by the Mughals, converted under Aurangzeb, and returned to Raigad in 1676 to be received back into the fold.
Son; accompanied him to Agra in 1666 and succeeded him in 1680.
Held Pavan Khind to the death on 13 July 1660 so he could reach Vishalgad safely.
Younger son; became the third Chhatrapati in 1689.
Half-brother; the two founded separate Maratha kingdoms at Satara and Thanjavur.
Bodyguard who saved his life at the Pratapgad parley by disabling Sayyed Banda.
Present at the Pratapgad parley; beheaded Afzal Khan after Shivaji struck him down.
Besieged him at Panhala in 1660, forcing his escape to Vishalgad.
Early trusted commander; died fighting the Mores of Jawli in his service.
Ran his intelligence network.
Chief secretary (Chitnis), drafting his official correspondence.
Negotiated the Golconda alliance and helped organize the 1677 Karnatak campaign.
Amatya (finance minister) in his Ashta Pradhan council of state.
Ambushed and defeated at Umberkhind in 1661.
Sultan of Bijapur who sent Afzal Khan against him in 1659.
Defeated him after he took command following his father Afzal Khan's death.
Wife; performed sati on his funeral pyre at Raigad.
Defeated near Kolhapur in December 1659.
Impersonated him in his palanquin for days after the 1666 Agra escape.
Helped plan and carry out his 1666 escape from Mughal custody at Agra.
Nyayadhish (chief justice) in his Ashta Pradhan council of state.
Took part in the 1665 Purandar siege that forced the treaty ceding 23 forts.
Eldest daughter; married her to Mahadji Nimbalkar as a political alliance.
Daughter; married her into the Jadhav family.

name: Shahaji Bhonsle
role: Maratha general in Deccan sultanate service
summary: Served the Ahmadnagar and then Bijapur sultanates as a general in the Deccan and Karnataka; father of Shivaji.

journey.label: Rises under Malik Ambar
journey.summary: Serves as a commander under the Ahmadnagar regent Malik Ambar; exact postings in these years are thinly recorded.

journey.label: Granted the Pune jagir under Bijapur
journey.summary: After Ahmadnagar falls to the Mughals, enters Bijapur service and is granted the Pune-Supe jagir, where he settles Jijabai and the young Shivaji.

journey.label: Takes up a Bijapur command in Karnataka
journey.summary: Spends most of his later career campaigning for Bijapur in Karnataka, based around Bangalore.
journey.routeNote: Day-to-day movements across these Karnataka campaigns are not finely dated in the works used here.

journey.label: Death in a hunting accident
journey.summary: Dies after a fall from his horse while hunting near Hodigere.
journey.routeNote: The precise site is given approximately; exact coordinates for Hodigere are not independently verified here.

relationships.note: Son; entered Bijapur service while Shivaji built an independent base around Pune.
Son by his second wife Tukabai; founded the Thanjavur Maratha kingdom.

name: Jijabai
role: Mother and early guide of Shivaji; regent during his minority
summary: Raised Shivaji at Pune while Shahaji campaigned in Karnataka, and lived to see his coronation in 1674, dying days afterward.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born to the Jadhav clan at Sindkhed Raja.

journey.label: Gives birth to Shivaji
journey.summary: Gives birth to Shivaji at Shivneri.

journey.label: Settles at Pune to raise Shivaji
journey.summary: Moves to the Pune jagir with the young Shivaji while Shahaji serves in Karnataka, and oversees his upbringing and early administration.

journey.label: Present at Shivaji's coronation
journey.summary: Lives to see her son crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Pachad, close to Raigad, within weeks of her son's coronation.

relationships.note: Son; raised and guided him at Pune while Shahaji served Bijapur.

name: Babur
summary: Timurid prince of Fergana who took Kabul in 1504 and Hindustan in 1526; author of the Bāburnāma.

relationships.note: Son; succeeded him as Mughal emperor in 1530.
Great-great-great-grandfather in the direct paternal line; the Mughal dynasty took its "Timurid" name from him.
Defeated and killed Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat, 1526, ending the Delhi Sultanate.

journey.label: First Battle of Panipat
journey.summary: Defeats the Delhi Sultanate under Ibrahim Lodi, founding the Mughal Empire.

journey.label: Battle of Khanwa
journey.summary: Defeats a Rajput confederacy under Rana Sanga of Mewar, securing the new empire.

name: Sher Shah Sur
summary: Afghan commander who expelled Humayun and reorganised revenue, coinage and roads. His birth year and birthplace are uncertain.

journey.label: Defeats Humayun at Chausa
journey.summary: Defeats Humayun at the Battle of Chausa.

journey.label: Defeats Humayun at Kannauj, founds the Sur Empire
journey.summary: Decisively defeats Humayun at Kannauj, forcing him into exile and founding the Sur Empire in place of Mughal rule.

journey.label: Death at the siege of Kalinjar
journey.summary: Dies from injuries in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of Kalinjar fort.

relationships.note: Defeated him at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540), forcing him into exile and founding the Sur Empire.

name: Akbar

namesakes.name: Akbar II
namesakes.note: Mughal emperor 1806–1837; son of Shah Alam II.

namesakes.name: Prince Muhammad Akbar
namesakes.note: Son of Aurangzeb who rebelled in 1681.

summary: Extended the empire across northern India and built its administrative system.

relationships.note: Father; succeeded him in 1556 at thirteen years old.
Regent and guardian for the first four years of the reign, dismissed in 1560.
Defeated and killed at the Second Battle of Panipat in 1556, securing the throne.
Mewar never submitted to him; fought to a standstill at Haldighati in 1576.
Rajput general and one of his closest nobles; commanded the Mughal force at Haldighati.
Son; succeeded him in 1605.
Grandfather; founded the empire Akbar would expand and consolidate.
Mewar continued resisting under Pratap’s son after Akbar’s own reign, finally submitting to Akbar’s son Jahangir in 1615.
Grand vizier and author of the Akbarnama, the official chronicle of his reign.
Finance minister who designed the empire's systematic land revenue settlement.
Court musician celebrated as one of the Navratnas of his court.
Close courtier; killed in 1586 leading an army against the Yusufzai tribes.
Leading general and poet at his court, holding the title Khan-i-Khanan.
Mother; lived to see most of his long reign.
Foster mother and dominant court power-broker during his minority.
Executed on his personal order in 1562 after murdering a rival minister.

journey.label: Accession
journey.summary: Enthroned at Kalanaur at age thirteen after Humayun’s death.

journey.label: Second Battle of Panipat
journey.summary: His regent Bairam Khan defeats Hemu, securing the throne.

journey.label: Falls of Chittorgarh
journey.summary: Besieges and takes Chittorgarh from Mewar.

journey.label: Founds Fatehpur Sikri
journey.summary: Founds the new capital of Fatehpur Sikri.

name: Maharana Pratap
summary: Refused submission to Akbar and held out in the Aravalli hills after Haldighati.

relationships.note: Refused to submit to Mughal overlordship; fought Akbar’s army to a standstill at Haldighati in 1576.
Father; succeeded him as ruler of Mewar in 1572.
Son; succeeded him in 1597 and continued the resistance for nearly two more decades.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at the hill fortress of Kumbhalgarh.

journey.label: Accession
journey.summary: Succeeds his father Udai Singh II as ruler of Mewar, crowned at Gogunda.

journey.label: Battle of Haldighati
journey.summary: Fights Akbar’s army under Man Singh I to a standstill at the pass of Haldighati; refuses to submit to Mughal overlordship.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Chavand, his later capital, having never submitted to the Mughal empire.

name: Jahangir
summary: Akbar’s son; kept a detailed memoir of his reign.

relationships.note: Father; succeeded him as emperor in 1605.
Accepted his submission in 1615, negotiated through Prince Khurram, ending Mewar’s decades-long resistance.

journey.label: Orders the execution of Guru Arjan
journey.summary: Orders the execution of the fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan, at Lahore.

journey.label: Receives Thomas Roe
journey.summary: Receives the English ambassador Thomas Roe at his court in Ajmer, opening formal relations with the English Crown.

name: Shah Jahan

namesakes.name: Shah Jahan II
namesakes.note: Emperor for a few months in 1719.

summary: Builder of the Taj Mahal and Shahjahanabad; deposed by his son Aurangzeb in 1658.

relationships.note: Wife; built the Taj Mahal as her tomb after her death in 1631.
Son; deposed him in 1658 and kept him confined at Agra Fort until his death.
Eldest son and designated heir; executed by Aurangzeb in 1659 after the war of succession.

journey.label: Death of Mumtaz Mahal
journey.summary: His wife Mumtaz Mahal dies at Burhanpur while accompanying him on campaign.

journey.label: Begins the Taj Mahal
journey.summary: Begins construction of the Taj Mahal at Agra as Mumtaz Mahal’s tomb.

journey.label: Inaugurates Shahjahanabad
journey.summary: Inaugurates Shahjahanabad, his new walled city at Delhi, as the Mughal capital.

name: Aurangzeb
summary: Ruled for 49 years and spent the last 25 campaigning in the Deccan.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at Dahod while Shah Jahan was travelling through Gujarat.

journey.label: First appointment as viceroy of the Deccan
journey.summary: Appointed to his first Deccan command under Shah Jahan, based near Daulatabad.
journey.routeNote: Movements of the 1620s-30s are not finely dated in the sources used here.

journey.label: Defeats Dara Shikoh at Samugarh
journey.summary: Decisive victory over his brother Dara Shikoh opens the way to the throne.

journey.label: Enthroned at Shahjahanabad
journey.summary: First, provisional coronation; a second, formal enthronement follows in 1659.

journey.label: Receives Shivaji at court
journey.summary: Presides over the audience that ends the Purandar settlement.

journey.label: Moves the court to the Deccan
journey.summary: Leads the imperial court south to campaign against Bijapur, Golconda and the Marathas; does not return north for the rest of his reign.

journey.label: Annexes Bijapur
journey.summary: Besieges and annexes the Adil Shahi sultanate of Bijapur.

journey.label: Annexes Golconda
journey.summary: Besieges and annexes the Qutb Shahi sultanate of Golconda.

journey.label: Besieges the Maratha fort of Jinji
journey.summary: Directs the prolonged, ultimately unsuccessful siege of Jinji in the far south.

journey.label: Personally besieges and takes Satara
journey.summary: Leads the siege of Satara in person, one of the last major Maratha forts he personally reduces.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies in camp at Ahmadnagar after close to two decades of continuous Deccan campaigning.

relationships.note: Received him at the 1666 Agra audience and placed him under guard; Shivaji escaped and remained a lasting Deccan adversary.
Maternal uncle, sent as viceroy of the Deccan.
Ordered his capture and execution at Tulapur in 1689.
Defeated him at Samugarh in 1658 and had him executed in 1659 in the war of succession.
Father; deposed and kept confined at Agra Fort from 1658 until his death in 1666.
Mother; died when he was twelve.
Fought his occupying armies in the Deccan from Jinji through most of the 1690s.
Continued the Maratha resistance against him as regent from 1700 until his death in 1707.
Ordered his execution at Delhi in 1675 for refusing to convert to Islam.
Forces loyal to his empire killed all four of Gobind Singh’s sons in 1704-05.
Son; later succeeded him as Emperor Bahadur Shah I.

name: Guru Gobind Singh
summary: Founded the Khalsa in 1699.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at Patna.

journey.label: Founds the Khalsa
journey.summary: Founds the Khalsa, the order of initiated Sikhs, at Anandpur Sahib on Vaisakhi.

journey.label: Loses two sons at Chamkaur
journey.summary: His elder sons Ajit Singh and Jujhar Singh are killed defending Chamkaur against a besieging Mughal and hill-chief force.

journey.label: Loses two more sons at Sirhind
journey.summary: His younger sons Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh are executed at Sirhind for refusing to convert to Islam.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Nanded from a wound inflicted by an assassin some days before.

relationships.note: Father; succeeded him as Guru at age nine after his execution in 1675.
Eldest son; died defending Chamkaur in 1704.
Second son; died defending Chamkaur in 1704.
Third son; executed at Sirhind in 1705.
Fourth son; executed at Sirhind in 1705.
His father Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed on Aurangzeb’s order in 1675; forces loyal to the Mughal empire and allied hill chiefs killed all four of his sons in 1704-05.

name: Baji Rao I
summary: Carried Maratha power north to Malwa, Bundelkhand and the outskirts of Delhi.

relationships.note: Son; succeeded him as Peshwa in 1720.
Son; succeeded him as Peshwa in 1740.

journey.label: Battle of Palkhed
journey.summary: Outmanoeuvres and defeats the Nizam of Hyderabad’s forces at Palkhed, a campaign often cited as a model of mobile warfare.

name: Robert Clive
role: East India Company commander and governor
summary: Commanded at Plassey and negotiated the diwani of Bengal.

relationships.note: Defeated him at Plassey on 23 June 1757, opening Bengal to Company control.

journey.label: Victory at Plassey
journey.summary: Defeats Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey on 23 June 1757, opening Bengal to Company control.

journey.label: Negotiates the Treaty of Allahabad
journey.summary: Negotiates the Treaty of Allahabad, securing the Mughal grant of the diwani (revenue administration) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa for the East India Company.

name: Tipu Sultan
summary: Fought the East India Company in three wars and died defending Srirangapatna. Some works give his birth as 1750.

relationships.note: Son; succeeded him as ruler of Mysore in December 1782, mid-war with the East India Company.

journey.label: Succeeds Hyder Ali
journey.summary: Succeeds his father as ruler of Mysore, mid-war with the East India Company.

journey.label: Death defending Srirangapatna
journey.summary: Dies defending his capital against a British-led siege in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

name: Ram Singh I of Amber
role: Mughal noble; Raja of Amber from 1667

namesakes.name: Sawai Ram Singh II of Jaipur
namesakes.note: Maharaja of Jaipur in the nineteenth century.

summary: Shivaji’s host and surety at Agra in 1666; later commanded the Mughal army defeated at Saraighat.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born into the Kachhwaha ruling house of Amber.

journey.label: Hosts and stands surety for Shivaji
journey.summary: As Shivaji's host at Agra, Ram Singh stands surety for his conduct at court.

journey.label: Succeeds as Raja of Amber
journey.summary: Succeeds his father Mirza Raja Jai Singh I.

journey.label: Commands the Mughal army at Saraighat
journey.summary: Leads the Mughal force defeated by the Ahom general Lachit Borphukan.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Kohat, on campaign on the Mughal empire's northwest frontier.
journey.routeNote: The circumstances of his final years on the frontier are thinly recorded in the works used here.

relationships.note: Son; succeeded him as ruler of Amber in 1667.
Stood surety for him at the 1666 Agra audience and sheltered him after the breach with Aurangzeb’s court.

name: Sambhaji

namesakes.name: Sambhaji II of Kolhapur
namesakes.note: Son of Rajaram; ruler of Kolhapur.

summary: Accompanied his father to Agra at the age of nine; succeeded him in 1680 and was executed on Aurangzeb’s order.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at Purandar fort to Shivaji and Saibai.

journey.label: Presented at court, aged nine
journey.summary: Travels to Agra with his father and is presented at Aurangzeb's court.

journey.label: Escapes Agra with his father
journey.summary: Slips out of guarded quarters with Shivaji; the method is not securely known.

journey.label: Crowned Chhatrapati
journey.summary: Crowned at Raigad after a succession dispute with his half-brother Rajaram's faction.

journey.label: Captured and executed
journey.summary: Captured at Sangameshwar and executed on Aurangzeb's order at Tulapur.
journey.routeNote: The route from capture at Sangameshwar to execution at Tulapur is not finely dated in the works used here.

relationships.note: Half-brother; succeeded him as Chhatrapati after his execution in 1689.
Son; held by the Mughals as a child after his execution, released in 1707.
Continued as Chitnis under Sambhaji and was executed alongside him by the Mughals in 1689.
As Mughal viceroy of the Deccan, Muazzam dealt directly with Sambhaji's Maratha kingdom.

name: Alexander of Macedon
summary: Reached the Beas in 326 BCE and turned back. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Battle of the Hydaspes
journey.summary: Defeats King Porus at the Hydaspes river, his last major battle, after which his own troops refuse to advance further into India.

relationships.note: Defeated him at the Hydaspes, then by most accounts reinstated him as a client ruler in recognition of his courage.

name: Porus
summary: Fought Alexander at the Hydaspes. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Battle of the Hydaspes
journey.summary: Fights Alexander’s army at the Hydaspes; defeated, but by most accounts reinstated as a client ruler in recognition of his courage.

relationships.note: Fought him at the Hydaspes; defeated, but reinstated as a client ruler afterward by most accounts.

name: Chandragupta Maurya
summary: Overthrew the Nandas and defeated Seleucus. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory. His own parentage is not settled: Buddhist tradition places him in the kshatriya Moriya clan, Jain and later Puranic accounts differ, and a later tradition connecting his mother to the Nanda court is not well substantiated. No single account is given here as fact.

relationships.note: Advised and, by tradition, engineered his overthrow of the Nanda dynasty c. 322 BCE; served as his chief minister afterward.
Son; succeeded him as Mauryan emperor.
Overthrew him to found the Maurya Empire, c. 322 BCE.

journey.label: Founds the Maurya Empire
journey.summary: Overthrows the Nanda dynasty, advised by Chanakya, and founds the Maurya Empire from the capital of Pataliputra.

name: Ashoka
summary: Left the edicts that are the main source for his reign. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Father.
Wife during his time as Mauryan viceroy at Vidisha.
Son; sent him to lead the Buddhist mission to Sri Lanka around 247 BCE.
Daughter; she followed Mahendra to Sri Lanka to found the order of Buddhist nuns there.

journey.label: The Kalinga War
journey.summary: Conquers Kalinga in a war so bloody that, by his own edicts, it leads him to renounce further conquest and promote Buddhist dhamma instead.

name: Harsha
summary: Host of the pilgrim Xuanzang. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Receives Xuanzang at court
journey.summary: Receives the Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Xuanzang at his court at Kannauj; Xuanzang’s own travel record becomes a major source for Harsha’s reign.

relationships.note: Hosted him at his court at Kannauj; Xuanzang’s travel account is a major source for Harsha’s reign.
Defeated by him around 618-619, one of Harsha’s few recorded military defeats.
Allied with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa; both hosted the pilgrim Xuanzang.

name: Xuanzang
summary: Travelled in India c. 630–643 and wrote the Records of the Western Regions. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Visits Harsha’s court
journey.summary: Visits the court of Harsha at Kannauj during his long pilgrimage across India, recording what he sees in his own travel account.

relationships.note: Hosted by him at Kannauj; recorded the visit in his own travel account, a major source for Harsha’s reign.

name: Mahmud of Ghazni
summary: Raided northern India seventeen times. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Sacks Somnath
journey.summary: Takes and plunders the temple town of Somnath, the most remembered of his seventeen raids into India.

relationships.note: Failed to subdue the Chandela king Vidyadhara, one of the few Indian rulers to repel his invasions.
Defeated Jayapala of the Hindu Shahi dynasty near Peshawar in 1001.

name: Rajaraja I
summary: Built the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Completes the Brihadeeswarar Temple
journey.summary: Completes the great Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur, one of the largest temples in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

relationships.note: Son; co-regent from 1012 and sole ruler from 1014, leading the dynasty to its furthest overseas reach.

name: Muhammad of Ghor
summary: Defeated Prithviraj at Tarain in 1192. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Defeated at the First Battle of Tarain
journey.summary: Defeated by Prithviraj Chauhan at the First Battle of Tarain.

journey.label: Victory at the Second Battle of Tarain
journey.summary: Defeats and kills Prithviraj Chauhan at the Second Battle of Tarain, opening North India to Ghurid conquest. Leaves his slave-general Qutb al-Din Aibak as viceroy in India.

journey.label: Assassination
journey.summary: Assassinated, by most accounts by rebels, while marching back toward Ghazni.

relationships.note: Defeated him at the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, then defeated and killed him at the Second in 1192.
Left him as viceroy of his Indian conquests; Aibak declared himself independent Sultan after his assassination in 1206.
Defeated and killed Jayachandra of Kannauj at the Battle of Chandawar, 1194.

name: Prithviraj III
summary: Lost to Muhammad of Ghor at Tarain. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Wins the First Battle of Tarain
journey.summary: Defeats Muhammad of Ghor’s invading army at the First Battle of Tarain.

journey.label: Defeat and death at the Second Battle of Tarain
journey.summary: Defeated, captured and killed at the Second Battle of Tarain, opening North India to the Ghurid conquest.

relationships.note: Defeated him at the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, then defeated and killed him at the Second in 1192.
Rival North Indian king; the two failed to unite against the Ghurid invasions.

name: Qutb al-Din Aibak
summary: Became ruler on Muhammad of Ghor’s death. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Viceroy in India
journey.summary: Left in charge of Muhammad of Ghor’s Indian conquests as his viceroy.

journey.label: Declares himself Sultan
journey.summary: Declares himself independent Sultan after Muhammad of Ghor’s assassination, founding the Delhi Sultanate (the Mamluk or Slave dynasty).

relationships.note: Served as his trusted general and viceroy in India before declaring independence after his death in 1206.

name: Alauddin Khalji
summary: Took Chittor in 1303. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Seizes the throne
journey.summary: Seizes the throne of the Delhi Sultanate after killing his uncle and father-in-law, Jalaluddin Khalji.

journey.label: Conquers Chittorgarh
journey.summary: Besieges and conquers the fortress of Chittorgarh.

journey.label: Conquers Ranthambore
journey.summary: Besieges and conquers the fortress of Ranthambore.

relationships.note: Forced the Yadava king of Devagiri to submit and pay tribute.
His 1304 invasion of Gujarat ended the Vaghela dynasty.

name: Muhammad bin Tughluq
summary: Moved the capital to Daulatabad in 1327. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Father; succeeded him in 1325.

journey.label: Moves the capital to Daulatabad
journey.summary: Orders the Delhi Sultanate’s capital moved from Delhi to Daulatabad, forcing much of the population to relocate; later reverses the decision.

name: Timur
summary: Sacked Delhi in 1398. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Sacks Delhi
journey.summary: Defeats Sultan Mahmud Tughluq outside Delhi; the city is plundered for days, and the Delhi Sultanate never recovers its former extent.

relationships.note: Great-great-great-grandfather in the direct paternal line; Babur founded the Mughal Empire as a Timurid prince more than a century after Timur’s own death.

name: Vasco da Gama
summary: Reached Calicut in 1498. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Reaches Calicut
journey.summary: Anchors off the Malabar coast after rounding Africa, opening the direct sea route between Europe and India.

relationships.note: Received by the Zamorin of Calicut in 1498; relations soured as the Portuguese pressed for a trade monopoly.

name: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi
summary: Led the Salt March in 1930; assassinated in 1948. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at Porbandar in Gujarat.

journey.label: Salt March
journey.summary: Completes the Dandi March and breaks the salt laws, launching the civil disobedience movement.

journey.label: Launches Quit India
journey.summary: Launches the Quit India movement, demanding an immediate end to British rule.

journey.label: Assassination
journey.summary: Assassinated at Birla House in Delhi on 30 January 1948.

relationships.note: Close political ally; launched the Quit India movement together in 1942.
Opposed his demand for a separate Pakistan, though the two negotiated repeatedly over the 1940s.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: Spoke at the midnight of 14–15 August 1947. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at Allahabad (Prayagraj).

journey.label: Quit India
journey.summary: Joins Gandhi in launching the Quit India movement; arrested shortly after.

journey.label: Independence - "Tryst with Destiny"
journey.summary: Delivers the "Tryst with Destiny" speech as India becomes independent and he becomes its first Prime Minister.

journey.label: Republic Day
journey.summary: Presides as Prime Minister as the Constitution of India comes into force.

relationships.note: Close political ally and eventual successor as leader of the independence movement.
Daughter; became Prime Minister herself in 1966.

name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
summary: Led the Muslim League to partition. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at Karachi.

journey.label: Governor-General of Pakistan
journey.summary: Becomes the first Governor-General of Pakistan on its independence, 14 August 1947.

relationships.note: Negotiated repeatedly with Gandhi over the 1940s before Partition; led the movement for a separate Pakistan.

name: Reginald Dyer
summary: Ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Jallianwala Bagh massacre
journey.summary: Orders troops to fire on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919, killing hundreds.

name: Ranjit Singh
summary: Ruled from Lahore from 1801. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

journey.label: Takes Lahore
journey.summary: Takes Lahore and begins uniting the Sikh misls into a single kingdom.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Lahore; the kingdom falls into succession disputes that end with British annexation a decade later.

relationships.note: Youngest son; became Maharaja as a child amid the succession disputes that followed his death, and lost the kingdom to British annexation in 1849.

name: Siraj-ud-Daulah
summary: Defeated at Plassey. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Defeated by his forces at Plassey on 23 June 1757; deposed and killed days later.

journey.label: Defeat at Plassey
journey.summary: Defeated by Robert Clive’s forces at Plassey on 23 June 1757, with key commanders bribed beforehand not to fight; deposed and killed days later.

name: Humayun
summary: Lost to Sher Shah at Chausa and Kannauj. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Father; founded the Mughal Empire that he inherited in 1530.
Son; succeeded him in 1556.
Defeated him at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540), forcing him into exile for fifteen years before he recaptured Delhi in 1555.
Wife; accompanied him through his years of exile in Persia.

journey.label: Defeat at Chausa
journey.summary: Defeated by Sher Shah Suri at Chausa.

journey.label: Decisive defeat, exile begins
journey.summary: Decisively defeated by Sher Shah Suri at Kannauj, beginning fifteen years of exile before he recaptures Delhi in 1555.

name: Bairam Khan
summary: Won the Second Battle of Panipat. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Served as his regent from 1556 to 1560, then was dismissed.
Son; raised at Akbar's court after his father's fall from power.

journey.label: Victory at the Second Battle of Panipat
journey.summary: Leads the Mughal army, as regent for the young Akbar, to victory over Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat.

name: Hemu
role: Hindu general of the Sur dynasty
summary: Captured Delhi in 1556, lost at Panipat. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Defeated and killed by Akbar’s forces at the Second Battle of Panipat, 5 November 1556.
Rose through the Sur administration he founded, eventually trying to restore Sur rule against Akbar.

journey.label: Defeat and death at the Second Battle of Panipat
journey.summary: Defeated and killed by the Mughal army under Bairam Khan at the Second Battle of Panipat, 5 November 1556.

name: Man Singh I of Amber
summary: Led the army at Haldighati. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Served as one of his leading generals; commanded the Mughal force at Haldighati in 1576.

journey.label: Commands at Haldighati
journey.summary: Commands the Mughal force that fights Maharana Pratap to a standstill at Haldighati.

name: Sadashivrao Bhau
summary: Commanded at the Third Battle of Panipat. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Commanded the Maratha army against him at the Third Battle of Panipat, 14 January 1761, and died in the defeat.
Cousin and Peshwa; sent him north to command at Panipat in his place.

journey.label: Death at the Third Battle of Panipat
journey.summary: Commands the Maratha army against Ahmad Shah Durrani at the Third Battle of Panipat, 14 January 1761, and dies in the defeat.

name: Ahmad Shah Durrani
summary: Won the Third Battle of Panipat. Lifespan approximate; entered from memory.

relationships.note: Defeated and killed him at the Third Battle of Panipat, 14 January 1761.
Fought him at the Third Battle of Panipat, 14 January 1761; Mahadji survived, wounded.

journey.label: Victory at the Third Battle of Panipat
journey.summary: Defeats the Maratha army under Sadashivrao Bhau at the Third Battle of Panipat, 14 January 1761.

name: Afzal Khan
summary: Senior Bijapur general sent in 1659 to put down Shivaji’s rising power; killed at a parley on Pratapgad on 10 November 1659. Birth year not attested; entered as an approximate estimate.

relationships.note: Marched on Pratapgad to capture or kill him; killed in the parley that followed.
Personal bodyguard who attacked Shivaji during the Pratapgad parley.
Sent by Ali Adil Shah II against Shivaji in 1659.
Son; took command of his Bijapur force after his death at Pratapgad.

journey.label: Sent against Shivaji
journey.summary: Dispatched from Bijapur with a large force to subdue Shivaji’s rising power in the Deccan hills.

journey.label: Death at the parley
journey.summary: Killed at a parley below Pratapgad fort on 10 November 1659; the Bijapur army is routed in the fighting that follows.
journey.routeNote: That he was killed at the meeting is certain; who struck first is disputed between Maratha and Bijapur-side accounts.

name: Shaista Khan
role: Mughal viceroy of the Deccan; later governor of Bengal
summary: Maternal uncle of Aurangzeb; occupied Pune as Mughal viceroy of the Deccan from 1660 until driven out by a night raid on his quarters in 1663. Later served as governor of Bengal.

relationships.note: Quartered at Pune (Lal Mahal) as occupying Mughal viceroy; wounded in the 1663 raid on his residence, which also killed a son.

journey.label: Occupies Pune as viceroy
journey.summary: Takes up residence at the Lal Mahal in Pune as Mughal viceroy of the Deccan, tasked with putting down Shivaji.

journey.label: Wounded in the night raid
journey.summary: Wounded, losing three fingers, when Shivaji’s men raid his quarters by night; a son is killed in the same raid. Recalled from the Deccan soon after.

journey.label: Governor of Bengal
journey.summary: Appointed governor of Bengal after his recall from the Deccan.

name: Mirza Raja Jai Singh I
role: Kachhwaha ruler of Amber; Mughal general
summary: Mughal general and ruler of Amber; led the 1665 campaign that besieged Purandar and brought Shivaji to terms, then escorted him to the 1666 audience at Agra.

relationships.note: Commanded the Mughal force that besieged Purandar in 1665; negotiated the treaty and later stood surety for the Agra visit.
Father.
Diler Khan joined his 1665 siege of Purandar.

journey.label: Besieges Purandar
journey.summary: Leads the Mughal campaign that besieges Purandar and forces the treaty ceding twenty-three forts to the empire.

journey.label: Escorts Shivaji to court
journey.summary: Stands surety for Shivaji’s safety at the Agra audience with Aurangzeb.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Burhanpur on the return march from the Deccan.

name: Tanaji Malusare
summary: Commander from Shivaji’s own household troops; led the night assault that retook the fort of Kondhana (Sinhagad) from the Mughals in February 1670 and died in the fighting. Birth year not attested; entered as an approximate estimate.

relationships.note: Childhood friend and trusted commander; died retaking Sinhagad on his order.

journey.label: Night assault on Sinhagad
journey.summary: Leads the night assault that retakes the fort of Kondhana (Sinhagad) from the Mughals on 4 February 1670; dies in the fighting.

name: Netaji Palkar
summary: Shivaji’s first commander-in-chief; captured by the Mughals in 1665–66, entered Mughal service as Muhammad Quli Khan, then returned to Raigad in 1676 where Shivaji had him ritually received back into Hindu society. Birth and death years not firmly attested; entered as approximate estimates.

relationships.note: Served as his first Sarnaubat before capture by the Mughals; returned to his service in 1676.

journey.label: Captured by the Mughals
journey.summary: Captured during the Mughal campaign against Shivaji’s forces.

journey.label: Converts under Aurangzeb
journey.summary: Converts to Islam and enters Mughal service as Muhammad Quli Khan, later serving on campaigns in the northwest.

journey.label: Returns to Shivaji
journey.summary: Returns to Raigad and is ritually received back into Hindu society on Shivaji’s order.

name: Dara Shikoh
role: Mughal prince; heir apparent to Shah Jahan
summary: Eldest son of Shah Jahan and his designated heir; a patron of comparative Sufi-Vedantic scholarship (his Majma-ul-Bahrain compares Islamic and Hindu mysticism). Defeated by Aurangzeb at Samugarh in 1658, captured in 1659, and executed on Aurangzeb’s order at Delhi.

relationships.note: Younger brother; defeated him at Samugarh in 1658 and had him executed in 1659 after capture.
Father’s designated heir; Shah Jahan was deposed and imprisoned by Aurangzeb before Dara’s execution could be prevented.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born at Ajmer, Shah Jahan’s eldest son.

journey.label: Defeat at Samugarh
journey.summary: Defeated by his brother Aurangzeb at Samugarh, opening the way to the throne for the younger brother.

journey.label: Execution
journey.summary: Captured after flight and executed on Aurangzeb’s order at Delhi.

name: Mumtaz Mahal
role: Mughal empress, consort of Shah Jahan
summary: Chief consort of Shah Jahan; died at Burhanpur giving birth to her fourteenth child. Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra as her mausoleum.

relationships.note: Husband; built the Taj Mahal as her tomb.
Mother.
Mother.

journey.label: Marriage to Shah Jahan
journey.summary: Married to Prince Khurram, the future Shah Jahan.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies at Burhanpur giving birth to her fourteenth child, while accompanying Shah Jahan on campaign in the Deccan.

name: Hyder Ali
summary: Rose through the Mysore army to become its de facto ruler by 1761, keeping the Wadiyar kings as figureheads. Fought the East India Company to a standstill in the First Anglo-Mysore War (1767–69) and was campaigning against it again when he died of cancer during the Second, in December 1782. Birth year not firmly attested; entered as an approximate estimate.

relationships.note: Father; Tipu succeeded him in December 1782, partway through the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

journey.label: De facto ruler of Mysore
journey.summary: Becomes the effective ruler of Mysore, keeping the Wadiyar kings as figureheads.

journey.label: Ends the First Anglo-Mysore War
journey.summary: Forces the East India Company to terms close to Madras, ending the first of the four Anglo-Mysore Wars.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Dies of cancer near Chittoor while campaigning in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

name: Balaji Vishwanath
role: First Peshwa of the Maratha Empire
summary: Appointed Peshwa (chief minister) by Chhatrapati Shahu in 1713. Negotiated the 1719 Mughal grant recognising Maratha rights to chauth and sardeshmukhi revenue across the six Deccan provinces, turning the Peshwa’s office into the Maratha state’s real centre of power.

relationships.note: Father; Bajirao succeeded him as Peshwa in 1720 at the age of twenty.
Appointed Peshwa by him in 1713.

journey.label: Appointed Peshwa
journey.summary: Appointed Peshwa by Chhatrapati Shahu.

journey.label: Secures the Mughal grant
journey.summary: Negotiates the Mughal grant recognising Maratha rights to chauth and sardeshmukhi revenue across the Deccan.

name: Baji Prabhu Deshpande
summary: Deshpande (hereditary revenue officer) of Hirdas Maval who took up arms for Shivaji. Held the narrow pass of Pavan Khind with a small rearguard on 13 July 1660 to cover Shivaji’s retreat from the siege of Panhala to Vishalgad, dying in the fighting after word reached him that Shivaji had reached safety. Birth year not attested; entered as an approximate estimate.

relationships.note: Died holding Pavan Khind on 13 July 1660 so he could reach Vishalgad safely during the retreat from Panhala.
His siege of Panhala set up the pursuit that Baji Prabhu's stand at Pavan Khind blocked.

journey.label: Deshpande of Hirdas Maval
journey.summary: Hereditary revenue officer of the Hirdas Maval who entered Shivaji’s service in the early years of the rising.

journey.label: Besieged at Panhala
journey.summary: Part of the garrison besieged by the Bijapur general Siddi Jauhar through the first half of 1660.

journey.label: Death holding the pass
journey.summary: Held the narrow pass with a small rearguard on 13 July 1660 to cover Shivaji’s retreat from Panhala to Vishalgad, dying in the fighting once word came that Shivaji had reached safety.
journey.routeNote: The retreat route from Panhala to Vishalgad via the pass is well attested; the pass itself was later named Pavan Khind ("sacred pass") for the stand.

name: Rajaram
summary: Younger son of Shivaji; placed on the throne at Raigad in 1689 after Sambhaji’s execution, then withdrew to the southern fort of Jinji (Gingee) and directed Maratha resistance to Aurangzeb’s occupying armies from there for most of the 1690s. Returned north and died at Sinhagad in 1700, still at war.

relationships.note: Father.
Half-brother; succeeded him as Chhatrapati after his execution in 1689.
Wife; led the Maratha resistance as regent after his death in 1700.
Directed Maratha resistance to his occupying armies from Jinji through most of the 1690s.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born to Shivaji and Soyarabai at Rajgad.

journey.label: Placed on the throne
journey.summary: Proclaimed Chhatrapati at Raigad after Sambhaji’s capture and execution.

journey.label: Withdraws to Jinji
journey.summary: Withdrew to the southern fortress of Jinji (Gingee) and directed Maratha resistance to Aurangzeb’s occupying armies from there through most of the 1690s.
journey.routeNote: The exact route south is not finely dated in the works used here.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Died at Sinhagad, still at war with the Mughal occupation.

name: Tarabai
summary: Widow of Rajaram; ruled as regent for their infant son Shivaji II and personally directed Maratha resistance to Aurangzeb after Rajaram’s death in 1700, continuing until the emperor’s own death in 1707. Opposed Shahu’s claim to the throne in the succession dispute that followed Aurangzeb’s withdrawal, and eventually headed a rival line based at Kolhapur. Lived into old age, re-entering Satara politics in her final years. Birth year not firmly attested; entered as an approximate estimate.

relationships.note: Husband; took up the regency and the war after his death in 1700.
Directed Maratha resistance to his occupation from 1700 until his death in 1707.
Defeated her forces at the Battle of Khed in 1707, taking the Satara throne she had been regent for.

journey.label: Married to Rajaram
journey.summary: Married to Rajaram; present at court during the crisis following Sambhaji’s execution.

journey.label: Takes up the regency
journey.summary: Took up the regency for their son Shivaji II after Rajaram’s death and directed the war against Aurangzeb’s occupation from the Maratha heartland until his death in 1707.
journey.routeNote: She moved between several forts directing the war; no single fixed seat is well attested for this period in the works used here.

journey.label: Rival court at Kolhapur
journey.summary: After Shahu’s victory at Khed in 1707 established his own line at Satara, her branch of the family held a separate court at Kolhapur.

name: Balaji Baji Rao
summary: Peshwa from 1740, continuing the northward expansion his father had begun. Sent the Maratha army north under his cousin Sadashivrao Bhau to confront Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1760; died at Pune a few weeks after news reached him of its destruction at the Third Battle of Panipat on 14 January 1761.

relationships.note: Father; he succeeded as Peshwa on Bajirao’s death in 1740.
Cousin, sent north in his place to command at the Third Battle of Panipat; died within weeks of the news of the defeat.

journey.label: Becomes Peshwa
journey.summary: Succeeds his father Bajirao I as Peshwa.

journey.label: Death after Panipat
journey.summary: Dies at Pune a few weeks after news reaches him of the destruction of the Maratha army at the Third Battle of Panipat.

name: Mahadji Scindia
role: Maratha military and political leader; ruler of Gwalior
summary: Survived the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, wounded and lamed for life, and spent the following decades rebuilding Maratha power in the north: recaptured Delhi in 1771, became the protector of the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II, and made Gwalior fort his base, founding the Scindia state there.

relationships.note: Fought and was wounded at the Third Battle of Panipat, 14 January 1761, which he survived.

journey.label: Wounded at Panipat
journey.summary: Fought at the Third Battle of Panipat on 14 January 1761; wounded and lamed for life in the defeat.

journey.label: Recaptures Delhi
journey.summary: Recaptured Delhi for the Marathas and became the protector of the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

journey.label: Makes Gwalior his base
journey.summary: Recaptured Gwalior fort and made it the base of the Scindia state.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Died near Pune at Wanowrie.

name: Shahu
summary: Son of Sambhaji; held in Mughal custody as a child from 1689 and released in 1707 after Aurangzeb’s death, a move meant to split the Marathas against Rajaram’s widow Tarabai. Defeated her forces at Khed in 1707 and ruled as Chhatrapati from Satara while Tarabai’s line held a rival court at Kolhapur. Appointed Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa in 1713, beginning the era in which the Peshwa’s office held the Maratha state’s real power.

relationships.note: Father; executed by Aurangzeb in 1689 when Shahu was a child.
Defeated her forces at the Battle of Khed in 1707 to establish his own claim to the throne at Satara, leaving her line a separate court at Kolhapur.
Appointed him Peshwa in 1713.

journey.label: Birth
journey.summary: Born to Sambhaji and Yesubai.

journey.label: Taken into Mughal custody
journey.summary: Captured with his mother Yesubai when Raigad fell to Mughal forces shortly after his father’s execution; held in the Mughal camp for the following eighteen years.

journey.label: Released and crowned
journey.summary: Released by Bahadur Shah I after Aurangzeb’s death; defeated Tarabai’s forces at Khed later that year and established his own court at Satara.

name: Murarbaji Deshpande
summary: Deshpande of Mazgaon and commander of the garrison at Purandar fort while Shivaji was elsewhere in 1665. Refused Diler Khan’s offer of honourable terms during the Mughal siege and led a sortie against the besiegers with a small force, dying in the fighting. Birth year not attested; entered as an approximate estimate.

relationships.note: Held Purandar against Diler Khan’s siege in 1665 while Shivaji was engaged elsewhere; died in a sortie rather than surrender the fort.
Killed defending Purandar against the Mughal siege Jai Singh directed in 1665.

journey.label: Commands the garrison
journey.summary: Commands the Maratha garrison at Purandar as the Mughal army under Diler Khan, part of Jai Singh’s campaign, lays siege to the fort.

journey.label: Death in the sortie
journey.summary: Refuses Diler Khan’s offer of honourable terms and leads a sortie against the besieging force; dies in the fighting.

name: Prataprao Gujar
summary: Appointed Sarnaubat after Netaji Palkar’s capture by the Mughals. Sent to intercept the retreating Bijapur general Bahlol Khan in early 1674, he let him go under truce on Shivaji’s standing orders, then on hearing Shivaji’s displeasure turned back and charged Bahlol Khan’s much larger force at Nesari with six companions, dying with them on 24 February 1674 — while Shivaji was at Raigad preparing for his coronation that June.

relationships.note: Served as his Sarnaubat; died charging Bahlol Khan’s army at Nesari in February 1674, months before Shivaji’s coronation at Raigad.
Succeeded him as Sarnaubat after his capture by the Mughals.

journey.label: Appointed Sarnaubat
journey.summary: Appointed commander-in-chief of the Maratha army after Netaji Palkar’s capture by the Mughals.

journey.label: Death at Nesari
journey.summary: Charges Bahlol Khan’s much larger retreating army with six companions after turning back on hearing of Shivaji’s displeasure at letting it go free; all die in the charge.

name: Hambirrao Mohite
summary: Related to Shivaji through his second wife Soyarabai, of the Mohite family. Succeeded Prataprao Gujar as Sarsenapati in 1674 and led the Maratha campaigns in the Karnatak and the Deccan through Shivaji’s later reign and into Sambhaji’s. Died in 1687 fighting the Mughal army under Sambhaji.

relationships.note: Succeeded Prataprao Gujar as Sarsenapati in 1674; led the southern Karnatak campaigns.
Continued as Sarsenapati into his reign; died fighting the Mughals in 1687.

journey.label: Appointed Sarsenapati
journey.summary: Succeeds Prataprao Gujar as commander-in-chief after his death at Nesari.

journey.label: Death in battle
journey.summary: Killed fighting a Mughal force during Sambhaji’s reign.

name: Yesaji Kank
summary: A companion of Shivaji from boyhood and one of his earliest mawla commanders, fighting alongside him from the first hill-fort campaigns of the 1640s. Took part in the storming of Sinhagad in 1670 alongside Tanaji Malusare. Death year not firmly attested.

relationships.note: Companion from boyhood; one of his earliest commanders.
Fellow commander at the storming of Sinhagad in 1670.

journey.label: Early hill-fort campaigns
journey.summary: Among Shivaji’s earliest companions in the first campaigns to take the hill forts around Pune.

journey.label: Storming of Sinhagad
journey.summary: Takes part in the night assault that retakes Sinhagad from the Mughals, alongside Tanaji Malusare.

name: Suryaji Malusare
summary: Younger brother of Tanaji Malusare. Took command of the assault on Sinhagad after Tanaji fell in the fighting on 4 February 1670, rallying the wavering Maratha troops to press on and take the fort. Death year not firmly attested.

relationships.note: Elder brother; took over command of the assault on Sinhagad after Tanaji fell, completing the capture of the fort.
Completed the capture of Sinhagad for him after Tanaji’s death in the assault.

journey.label: Takes command after Tanaji’s death
journey.summary: Rallies the Maratha troops and completes the capture of Sinhagad after his brother Tanaji is killed in the assault.

name: Moropant Pingle
summary: Shivaji’s Peshwa, the senior minister of the eight-member council (Ashta Pradhan), handling administration and sometimes leading campaigns in his own right while Shivaji was occupied elsewhere. Continued in office into the early part of Sambhaji’s reign.

relationships.note: Served as his Peshwa, running administration and leading campaigns independently while Shivaji was engaged elsewhere.
Continued in office as Peshwa into the early part of his reign.

journey.label: Peshwa at the coronation
journey.summary: Senior minister of the Ashta Pradhan council at Shivaji’s coronation as Chhatrapati.

name: Malharrao Holkar
summary: Rose from a shepherd family in Wagaj to become one of the Peshwa’s senior commanders, granted a jagir covering Indore and much of Malwa that became the Holkar state. Fought in most of the major Maratha campaigns of his generation, survived the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, and remained a major power broker in Maratha politics until his death in 1766.

relationships.note: Rose to prominence as one of his field commanders during the Malwa campaigns.
Fought at the Third Battle of Panipat, 14 January 1761, and survived.

journey.label: Campaigns in Malwa
journey.summary: Serves as a field commander in the Peshwa’s campaigns across Malwa, the region that becomes his own base.

journey.label: Survives Panipat
journey.summary: Present at the Third Battle of Panipat on 14 January 1761 and survives the defeat.

name: Ranoji Scindia
summary: Began in Peshwa Bajirao I’s personal service and rose to military command, granted a jagir in Malwa that became the Scindia state. Made Ujjain his capital. Father of Mahadji Scindia, who later moved the family’s base to Gwalior.

relationships.note: Began in his personal service before rising to independent military command in Malwa.
Father; Mahadji later moved the family’s base from Ujjain to Gwalior.

journey.label: Granted a command in Malwa

name: Chanakya
role: Philosopher-statesman; chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya
summary: Traditionally credited as the strategist behind Chandragupta Maurya’s overthrow of the Nanda dynasty and the founding of the Maurya Empire around 322 BCE, after which he served as chief advisor. Traditionally identified as the author of the Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft and political economy, though its date and single authorship are debated among scholars. Much of his biography comes from later and partly legendary sources (the Vishnu Purana, the Sanskrit drama Mudrarakshasa) rather than strictly contemporary record; dates entered here are approximate scholarly estimates.

name: Bindusara
summary: Son of Chandragupta Maurya and the second Mauryan emperor, ruling c. 297–273 BCE. Continued the empire’s southward expansion and maintained diplomatic relations with the Hellenistic kingdoms to the west, who knew him as Amitrochates; the Greek writer Deimachus served as ambassador at his court. Father of Ashoka.

name: Mahendra
role: Buddhist monk; led the mission that brought Buddhism to Sri Lanka
summary: Son of Ashoka and Devi. Ordained as a Buddhist monk and led the mission, after the Third Buddhist Council, that introduced Buddhism to Sri Lanka under King Devanampiya Tissa around 247 BCE. Remained in Sri Lanka for the rest of his life.

name: Sanghamitra
role: Buddhist nun; established the order of nuns in Sri Lanka
summary: Daughter of Ashoka and Devi. Followed her brother Mahendra to Sri Lanka, bringing a sapling of the Bodhi tree, and established the order of Buddhist nuns (bhikkhuni sangha) there.

name: Kunala
role: Mauryan prince, heir apparent to Ashoka
summary: Son of Ashoka and heir apparent. By the tradition recorded in the Buddhist Ashokavadana, blinded through the intrigue of a stepmother, Tishyarakshita, and set aside from the succession; the throne passed instead to his own son Samprati. The story’s details vary between the Buddhist and Jain traditions that preserve it, and are not corroborated by a contemporary Mauryan record.

relationships.note: Father; his heir apparent until set aside from the succession.
Father; the throne passed to Samprati instead of him.

name: Samprati
summary: Grandson of Ashoka, succeeding to the Mauryan throne after his father Kunala was set aside from the succession. In Jain tradition he is remembered as a great patron of Jainism, comparable to Ashoka’s patronage of Buddhism, credited with temple-building across the empire; this tradition is considerably later than his own lifetime and not corroborated by a contemporary record. The succession and dates of the later Mauryan emperors are poorly attested and vary between the surviving king-lists.

relationships.note: Father; the throne passed to him after Kunala was set aside from the succession.

name: Vallabhbhai Patel
role: Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India
summary: India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister, known as the "Iron Man of India" for overseeing the integration of more than five hundred princely states into the Indian Union between 1947 and 1949, including Hyderabad’s accession by force (Operation Polo, September 1948) and Junagadh’s.

name: Subhas Chandra Bose
role: Founder of the Indian National Army
summary: Congress leader who broke with Gandhi’s non-violent strategy, escaped house arrest in 1941, and organised the Indian National Army with Axis support during the Second World War to fight British rule by force. Reported to have died in a plane crash at Taipei on 18 August 1945; the circumstances of his death have long been disputed and remain a subject of ongoing debate rather than settled fact.

name: B. R. Ambedkar
role: Chief architect of the Constitution of India
summary: Chairman of the Constitution Drafting Committee and the chief architect of the Constitution of India, adopted in 1949. A leader of the Dalit rights movement throughout his life, he converted to Buddhism along with several hundred thousand followers at Nagpur in October 1956, a few weeks before his death.

summary: Younger son of Indira and Feroze Gandhi, and her political heir apparent during and after the Emergency, overseeing controversial programmes including a forced sterilisation drive. name: Udai Singh II
role: Ruler of Mewar; founder of Udaipur
summary: Ruler of Mewar who founded the city of Udaipur in 1559 as a new capital, judging Chittorgarh too exposed to Mughal attack. summary: Succeeded his father Pratap as ruler of Mewar in 1597 and continued the resistance to Mughal overlordship for nearly two decades, before submitting to Prince Khurram (the future Shah Jahan) in 1615 - ending more than forty years of continuous Mewar resistance that had begun under Udai Singh II and Pratap, while retaining internal autonomy within the empire.

summary: Ninth Sikh Guru. Executed at Delhi on Aurangzeb’s order on 11 November 1675 for refusing to convert to Islam, after interceding on behalf of a group of Kashmiri Pandits who had sought his protection against forced conversion.

name: Bimbisara

summary: King of Magadha, ruling from Rajagriha (Rajgir), and a contemporary and patron of both the Buddha and Mahavira according to Buddhist and Jain tradition. summary: Son of Bimbisara; by Buddhist tradition took the throne of Magadha by imprisoning and killing his father. Conquered the Vajji confederacy, including Vaishali, after a long war, and fortified a village called Pataligrama on the Ganges that would later grow into the city of Pataliputra, Magadha’s imperial capital under the Mauryas.

Overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya, advised by Chanakya, around 322 BCE, ending the dynasty his father had founded.

name: Prasenajit
summary: King of Kosala, ruling from Shravasti; a patron of the Buddha and a contemporary of Bimbisara of Magadha, by Buddhist tradition. By the same tradition, deposed in old age by his own son Vidudabha, who went on to attack the Buddha’s own Shakya clan.

name: Chanda Pradyota
