summary: Overthrew the Chalukyas of Badami around 753 CE to found the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the Deccan. The dynasty he founded would later build the great Kailasa rock-cut temple at Ellora under his successors.

journey.label: Overthrows the Chalukyas of Badami
journey.summary: Overthrows the Chalukyas of Badami, founding the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the Deccan.

name: Narasimhavarman I
summary: The most celebrated Pallava king, reigning c. 630-668 CE. Defeated the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II and, by tradition, sacked the Chalukya capital Vatapi (Badami) in revenge for an earlier Chalukya invasion of Pallava territory. Built the Shore Temple and the rock-cut monuments at Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram).

relationships.note: Defeated him and, by tradition, sacked the Chalukya capital Vatapi in revenge for an earlier invasion.

journey.label: Builds the Shore Temple and rock-cut monuments
journey.summary: Builds the Shore Temple and the rock-cut monuments at Mamallapuram, which still stand today.

name: Pulakeshin II
summary: Chalukya king of Badami (Vatapi), reigning 610-642 CE. Famously repelled an invasion by Harsha of Kanauj around 618-619, one of the few recorded defeats of Harsha’s army, and exchanged embassies with the Persian Sasanian court. Defeated and killed by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I, who by tradition sacked his capital in revenge for an earlier Chalukya invasion.

relationships.note: Repelled his invasion around 618-619, one of the few recorded defeats of Harsha’s army.
Defeated and killed by him; his capital Vatapi was sacked in revenge for an earlier Chalukya invasion of Pallava territory.

journey.label: Repels Harsha’s invasion
journey.summary: Repels an invasion by Harsha of Kanauj, one of the few recorded defeats of Harsha’s army.

journey.label: Death
journey.summary: Defeated and killed when the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I sacks his capital, Vatapi.

name: Vishnuvardhana
summary: The most significant early Hoysala king, reigning 1108-1152 CE. Originally Jain, converted to Vaishnavism under the influence of the philosopher Ramanuja and built the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur to commemorate a military victory.

journey.label: Builds the Chennakeshava Temple
journey.summary: Builds the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur to commemorate a military victory.

name: Yusuf Adil Shah
role: Founder of the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur
summary: Founded the Adil Shahi dynasty at Bijapur in 1490, breaking away from the declining Bahmani Sultanate to establish one of the independent Deccan sultanates.

journey.label: Founds the Adil Shahi dynasty
journey.summary: Breaks away from the declining Bahmani Sultanate to found the Adil Shahi dynasty at Bijapur.

name: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah
role: Founder of the Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda
summary: Founded the Qutb Shahi dynasty at Golconda in 1518, breaking away from the declining Bahmani Sultanate to establish one of the independent Deccan sultanates. Strengthened the fortress of Golconda.

journey.label: Founds the Qutb Shahi dynasty
journey.summary: Breaks away from the declining Bahmani Sultanate to found the Qutb Shahi dynasty at Golconda.

name: Gopala
summary: Elected by Bengali chieftains to end a period of anarchy (matsyanyaya); founded the Pala dynasty that came to dominate Bengal and Bihar for four centuries.

relationships.note: Father; succeeded by him as Pala ruler.

journey.label: Elected ruler of Bengal
journey.summary: Chosen by regional chieftains to restore order after a period of political anarchy, founding the Pala dynasty.

name: Dharmapala
summary: Expanded the Pala Empire to its greatest extent, contesting Kannauj with the Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas; founded the Buddhist university of Vikramashila.

relationships.note: Father; founder of the dynasty.
Contested control of Kannauj in the three-way "Kannauj triangle" struggle.

journey.label: Founds Vikramashila monastery
journey.summary: Establishes the Buddhist monastic university of Vikramashila, which became a leading center of Buddhist learning.

journey.label: Installs a client king at Kannauj
journey.summary: Intervenes in Kannauj during the prolonged tripartite struggle between the Palas, Pratiharas, and Rashtrakutas for control of the Gangetic heartland.

name: Ala-ud-Din Hasan Bahman Shah
summary: A Delhi Sultanate officer in the Deccan who led a rebellion and in 1347 established the independent Bahmani Sultanate at Gulbarga, the first major Muslim kingdom of the Deccan.

journey.label: Crowned Sultan at Gulbarga
journey.summary: Proclaimed independent sultan after the Deccan amirs rebelled against Delhi, founding the Bahmani dynasty with Gulbarga (Ahsanabad) as capital.

name: Bahlul Khan Lodi
role: Founder of the Lodi dynasty, Sultan of Delhi
summary: An Afghan noble who deposed the last Sayyid sultan in 1451 and founded the Lodi dynasty, the last Afghan dynasty to rule the Delhi Sultanate.

relationships.note: Son; succeeded him as Sultan of Delhi.

journey.label: Seizes the throne of Delhi
journey.summary: Deposes the Sayyid sultan Alam Shah and takes the throne of Delhi, founding the Lodi dynasty.

name: Sikandar Lodi
summary: Son of Bahlul Lodi; consolidated the Lodi sultanate, founded Agra as a capital, and strengthened administration before his death in 1517.

relationships.note: Father; founder of the Lodi dynasty.
Son; succeeded him as Sultan of Delhi.

journey.label: Founds Agra as a capital
journey.summary: Establishes Agra as a seat of government, strengthening Lodi control over the Gangetic-Yamuna plain.

name: Ibrahim Lodi
role: Last Sultan of Delhi of the Lodi dynasty
summary: Last Lodi Sultan of Delhi; alienated many of his own Afghan nobles, one of whom (Daulat Khan Lodi) invited Babur into India. Killed at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, ending the Delhi Sultanate and opening the way for the Mughal Empire.

relationships.note: Father; preceded him as Sultan of Delhi.
Defeated and killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat, 1526.

journey.label: Killed at the First Battle of Panipat
journey.summary: Dies fighting Babur's invading army at Panipat; his death ends the Delhi Sultanate and the Lodi dynasty.

name: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I
role: Founder of the Hyderabad State (Nizams of Hyderabad)
summary: A Mughal general and viceroy of the Deccan who, as Mughal central authority collapsed, established himself as the effectively independent ruler of Hyderabad in 1724, founding the Asaf Jahi dynasty of Nizams.

journey.label: Establishes autonomous rule in Hyderabad
journey.summary: Defeats a rival Mughal-appointed governor and establishes de facto independent rule over the Deccan from Hyderabad, founding the Asaf Jahi dynasty.

name: Afonso de Albuquerque
summary: Second governor of Portuguese India; captured Goa in 1510, making it the capital of the Estado da India, and built the fortified trading-post empire that anchored Portuguese power in Asia for a century.

journey.label: Captures Goa
journey.summary: Seizes Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate, making it the capital of the Estado da India and the base of Portuguese power in Asia.

name: Rudradaman I
role: Western Kshatrapa ruler of Saurashtra and Malwa
summary: Greatest ruler of the Western Kshatrapa (Saka) dynasty; defeated the Satavahanas twice and restored the Sudarshana lake dam near Girnar. Commemorated in the Junagadh rock inscription, the earliest long inscription in classical Sanskrit.

journey.label: Junagadh rock inscription
journey.summary: Records the repair of the Sudarshana dam and his military victories in the earliest surviving long inscription composed in classical Sanskrit.

name: Gautamiputra Satakarni
role: Greatest ruler of the Satavahana dynasty
summary: Restored Satavahana power in the Deccan, defeating the Western Kshatrapa ruler Nahapana and claiming to have destroyed the Shakas, Yavanas, and Pahlavas. Celebrated in his mother Gautami Balashri’s Nashik cave inscription.

relationships.note: Satavahana-Western Kshatrapa rivalry over the Deccan and western India; Gautamiputra defeated Rudradaman’s predecessor Nahapana, though Rudradaman later recovered the lost territory.

journey.label: Rules from the Satavahana capital Pratishthana
journey.summary: Governs the restored Satavahana realm from the capital Pratishthana (Paithan) after defeating the Western Kshatrapas.

name: Siddharaja Jayasimha
summary: Greatest ruler of the Chaulukya (Solanki) dynasty of Gujarat; expanded the kingdom from his capital Anhilwara (Patan), patronized Jain and Shaiva scholars, and built the Rudra Mahalaya temple.

relationships.note: Succeeded by his cousin Kumarapala, who continued Chaulukya rule from Anhilwara.

journey.label: Rules from Anhilwara (Patan)
journey.summary: Governs the Chaulukya kingdom of Gujarat from the capital Anhilwara, at the height of its power.

name: Kumarapala
summary: Succeeded his cousin Siddharaja Jayasimha as Chaulukya king of Gujarat; famously patronized the Jain scholar Hemachandra and promoted Jain religious practice across the kingdom.

relationships.note: Cousin and predecessor as Chaulukya king.

journey.label: Rules from Anhilwara (Patan)
journey.summary: Rules the Chaulukya kingdom from Anhilwara, patronizing the Jain scholar Hemachandra.

name: Jayachandra
role: Last major Gahadavala king of Kannauj
summary: Last powerful Gahadavala ruler of Kannauj; defeated and killed by Muhammad of Ghor at the Battle of Chandawar in 1194, a defeat that, together with Prithviraj Chauhan’s fall at Tarain, opened North India to Ghurid conquest.

relationships.note: Defeated and killed by Muhammad of Ghor at the Battle of Chandawar, 1194.
Rival North Indian king; the two failed to unite against the Ghurid invasions.

journey.label: Defeated and killed at Chandawar
journey.summary: Dies fighting Muhammad of Ghor's forces near Kannauj, ending major Gahadavala power in North India.

name: Mahmud Begada
summary: Greatest sultan of the Gujarat Sultanate; conquered the Rajput forts of Girnar and Champaner and the pilgrimage port of Dwarka, building Gujarat into the dominant power of western India.

journey.label: Rules the Gujarat Sultanate
journey.summary: Governs the Gujarat Sultanate at its height, after conquering Champaner and Girnar and extending control to the coast.

name: Sukaphaa
summary: Tai prince who led his followers across the Patkai hills from Mong Mao into the Brahmaputra valley and founded the Ahom Kingdom in 1228, beginning six centuries of Ahom rule in Assam.

journey.label: Founds the Ahom Kingdom
journey.summary: Establishes his first capital at Charaideo after crossing into the Brahmaputra valley, founding the Ahom Kingdom.

name: Menander I
role: Greatest king of the Indo-Greek kingdoms
summary: Most powerful Indo-Greek ruler, expanding Greek rule deep into northern India from his capital Sagala; remembered in Indian tradition as "Milinda," whose dialogues with the Buddhist monk Nagasena are recorded in the Pali text Milinda Panha.

journey.label: Rules the Indo-Greek kingdom from Sagala
journey.summary: Governs the Indo-Greek kingdom from his capital Sagala (modern Sialkot) at the height of Greek rule in India.

name: Vikramaditya VI
role: Greatest ruler of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani
summary: Longest-reigning and most powerful Western Chalukya king, ruling the Deccan from Kalyani for fifty years; began his own Chalukya-Vikrama era calendar still referenced in later Deccan inscriptions.

journey.label: Rules the Western Chalukya empire from Kalyani
journey.summary: Governs the Western Chalukya empire from the capital Kalyani at the height of its power in the Deccan.

name: Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I
role: Reviver of Pandya power in South India
summary: Revived the Pandya dynasty’s power after centuries of Chola dominance, conquering Chola territory, extending influence into Sri Lanka, and making Madurai the center of a renewed Pandya empire.

journey.label: Revives Pandya power from Madurai
journey.summary: Rules a resurgent Pandya empire from Madurai after defeating the weakened Chola kingdom.

name: Hoshang Shah
role: Founder of the independent Malwa Sultanate
summary: Established the independent Malwa Sultanate after his father broke away from Delhi; made Mandu his capital and built it into a major fortified city, where his own marble tomb still stands.

journey.label: Makes Mandu the Malwa capital
journey.summary: Establishes Mandu as the fortified capital of the independent Malwa Sultanate.

name: Vidyadhara
summary: Most powerful Chandela king, famed for successfully resisting an invasion by Mahmud of Ghazni; ruled from Khajuraho and Mahoba during the dynasty’s temple-building peak.

relationships.note: Repelled an invasion by Mahmud of Ghazni's forces, one of the few Indian rulers of the era to do so.

journey.label: Resists Mahmud of Ghazni’s invasion
journey.summary: Rules the Chandela kingdom from Khajuraho and successfully fends off an invasion by Mahmud of Ghazni.

name: Narasimhadeva I
summary: Eastern Ganga king who defeated an invading Bengal Sultanate army and built the Sun Temple at Konark to commemorate the victory, one of the great architectural monuments of medieval India.

journey.label: Builds the Sun Temple at Konark
journey.summary: Commissions the Sun Temple at Konark to commemorate his victory over an invading army, one of the masterpieces of Odishan temple architecture.

name: Pukkusati
summary: King of Gandhara named in the early Buddhist Pali canon as a contemporary and ally of Bimbisara of Magadha, with whom he exchanged embassies; one of the few named rulers of a Mahajanapada attested before Chanakya’s era.

relationships.note: Contemporary kings who exchanged embassies, per the early Buddhist canon.

journey.label: Rules Gandhara from Taxila
journey.summary: Governs the Mahajanapada of Gandhara, exchanging embassies with Bimbisara of distant Magadha.

name: Chetaka
role: Lichchhavi chief of the Vajji confederacy
summary: Head of the Lichchhavi clan of Vaishali and a leading figure of the Vajji confederacy, an early republic; maternal uncle of Mahavira in Jain tradition, and grandfather of Ajatashatru’s rival claims over Vaishali that led to its eventual fall to Magadha.

relationships.note: The Vajji confederacy he led was eventually conquered by Ajatashatru of Magadha.

journey.label: Leads the Vajji confederacy from Vaishali
journey.summary: Heads the Lichchhavi clan at Vaishali, the capital of the Vajji confederacy, one of the earliest known republics.

name: Muhammad bin Qasim
summary: Umayyad general who conquered the Hindu kingdom of Sindh in 712 CE, defeating and killing Raja Dahir at Aror; established the first lasting Muslim rule on the Indian subcontinent.

journey.label: Conquers Sindh, defeats Raja Dahir
journey.summary: Defeats and kills Raja Dahir at Aror, establishing Umayyad rule over Sindh.

name: Jayapala
role: King of the Hindu Shahi dynasty
summary: Hindu Shahi king who repeatedly resisted the Ghaznavid advance into the Punjab, fighting both Sabuktigin and his son Mahmud of Ghazni before being defeated near Peshawar in 1001 and dying by self-immolation.

relationships.note: Defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni near Peshawar in 1001, after which he died by self-immolation rather than live in defeat.

journey.label: Defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni
journey.summary: Defeated near Peshawar by Mahmud of Ghazni; dies by self-immolation rather than accept the humiliation of defeat.

name: Lakshmana Sena
role: Last major Sena king of Bengal
summary: Last powerful ruler of the Sena dynasty of Bengal; fled his capital Nadia without a fight when Bakhtiyar Khalji’s cavalry raided it around 1204–1205, an event marking the start of Muslim rule in Bengal.

journey.label: Flees before Bakhtiyar Khalji’s raid
journey.summary: Abandons his Bengal capital before an advancing Turkic cavalry raid, ending major Sena power in Bengal.

name: Rudrama Devi
summary: Ruled the Kakatiya kingdom of Warangal in her own right as one of the few women to rule a major Indian kingdom; successfully defended it against Yadava and Delhi Sultanate incursions, and was described by Marco Polo, who passed through the region.

journey.label: Rules the Kakatiya kingdom
journey.summary: Governs the Kakatiya kingdom from Warangal, defending it against external attack.

name: Lalitaditya Muktapida
role: Greatest king of the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir
summary: Most powerful ruler of early Kashmir, leading wide-ranging military campaigns across northern India and Central Asia; built the Martand Sun Temple. His reign is the centerpiece of Kalhana’s twelfth-century chronicle Rajatarangini.

journey.label: Rules Kashmir at its medieval peak
journey.summary: Governs the Kashmir valley at the height of Karkota power, before campaigning widely across northern India.

name: Rao Jodha
role: Founder of Jodhpur, Rathore ruler of Marwar
summary: Rathore chief who founded the fortress city of Jodhpur in 1459 as the new capital of Marwar, replacing the older seat at Mandore.

relationships.note: Son; left Marwar to found his own state at Bikaner.

journey.label: Founds Jodhpur
journey.summary: Founds Mehrangarh fort and the city of Jodhpur as the new Rathore capital of Marwar.

name: Gulab Singh
role: Founder of the Dogra dynasty of Jammu and Kashmir
summary: Dogra general in Sikh service who, after the First Anglo-Sikh War, purchased the Kashmir valley from the British under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) and founded the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.

journey.label: Founds the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir
journey.summary: Acquires Kashmir from the British East India Company under the Treaty of Amritsar, becoming the first Dogra Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.

name: Marthanda Varma
role: Founder of the modern state of Travancore
summary: Transformed Travancore from a minor Kerala chiefdom into a major regional power, defeating the Dutch East India Company at the Battle of Colachel in 1741 — one of the first Asian victories over a European colonial power — and consolidating control over southern Kerala.

journey.label: Defeats the Dutch at Colachel
journey.summary: Defeats the Dutch East India Company at Colachel, securing Travancore’s independence from European military pressure.

name: Malik Ambar
role: Regent and military leader of Ahmadnagar
summary: Abyssinian-born former slave who rose to become the de facto ruler of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate, using guerrilla tactics and a mobile revenue-raiding strategy to resist Mughal annexation of the Deccan for over two decades — methods later echoed by Shivaji.

journey.label: Leads Ahmadnagar’s resistance to the Mughals
journey.summary: Directs Ahmadnagar’s guerrilla resistance to Mughal expansion in the Deccan from the fortress of Ahmadnagar.

name: Mayurasharma
summary: Brahmin scholar who, after a dispute over his standing at the Pallava court, raised an army and founded the Kadamba dynasty at Banavasi around 345 CE — one of the earliest native Kannada-speaking dynasties, recorded in the Talagunda inscription.

journey.label: Founds the Kadamba dynasty
journey.summary: Establishes the Kadamba dynasty at Banavasi, per the Talagunda pillar inscription.

name: Cheran Chenguttuvan
role: Most celebrated king of the Sangam-era Chera kingdom
summary: Chera king of the Sangam age celebrated in the Tamil epic Silappatikaram for consecrating a temple to Kannagi, deified as the goddess Pattini; his campaigns are described in classical Tamil Sangam poetry.

journey.label: Rules the Chera kingdom from Karur (Vanji)
journey.summary: Governs the Chera kingdom from the capital region of Karur, celebrated in Sangam-era Tamil poetry.

name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
summary: Led the Bengali nationalist movement in East Pakistan and declared the independence of Bangladesh in 1971; became its first president and, later, prime minister, before being assassinated in a 1975 coup.

journey.label: Declares the independence of Bangladesh
journey.summary: Leads the movement that declares Bangladesh’s independence from Pakistan in 1971, becoming its founding leader.

name: Bhaskaravarman
summary: King of Kamarupa (ancient Assam) and ally of Harsha of Kannauj; hosted the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang at his court, who left a detailed account of the kingdom.

relationships.note: Allied with Harsha of Kannauj; both hosted the pilgrim Xuanzang.

journey.label: Hosts the pilgrim Xuanzang
journey.summary: Receives the Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Xuanzang at his Kamarupa court, who records his kingdom in detail.

name: Kapilendra Deva
role: Founder of the Gajapati dynasty of Odisha
summary: Founded the Gajapati dynasty after the decline of the Eastern Ganga line, expanding Odishan power south into the Vijayanagara and Bahmani borderlands.

journey.label: Founds the Gajapati dynasty
journey.summary: Takes the Odishan throne and founds the Gajapati dynasty, expanding its territory south and west.

name: Manavikraman Raja
summary: Hereditary Zamorin of Calicut who received Vasco da Gama at his court in 1498, the first direct contact between a Portuguese expedition and an Indian ruler — initially cordial, later souring into conflict as the Portuguese tried to monopolize the spice trade.

relationships.note: Received Vasco da Gama at Calicut in 1498; relations soured as the Portuguese pressed for a trade monopoly.

journey.label: Receives Vasco da Gama at Calicut
journey.summary: Receives Vasco da Gama's expedition at his court, the first direct contact between Portugal and India.

name: Darius I
summary: Achaemenid Great King who annexed Gandhara and the Indus valley as a satrapy of the Persian Empire, the first time the northwest of the subcontinent was absorbed into a transcontinental empire, recorded in his own Behistun and Persepolis inscriptions.

journey.label: Annexes the Indus valley satrapy
journey.summary: Brings Gandhara and the Indus valley into the Achaemenid Empire as a satrapy, per his own Persepolis inscriptions.

name: Alauddin Husain Shah
summary: Founded the Husain Shahi dynasty of the independent Bengal Sultanate; his reign is remembered as a golden age of Bengali literature and relative religious tolerance.

journey.label: Rules independent Bengal from Gaur
journey.summary: Governs the independent Bengal Sultanate from Gaur during a period of cultural flourishing.

name: Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
role: Sultan of the independent Jaunpur Sultanate
summary: Ruler of the independent Sharqi Sultanate of Jaunpur, which broke away from Delhi; made Jaunpur a renowned center of Islamic learning and architecture, earning it the title "Shiraz of the East."

journey.label: Builds Jaunpur into a center of learning
journey.summary: Rules the independent Jaunpur Sultanate, patronizing scholarship and architecture.

name: Prabhavatigupta
role: Vakataka queen regent, daughter of Chandragupta II
summary: Daughter of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II, married into the Vakataka dynasty of the Deccan; ruled as regent for her minor sons after her husband Rudrasena II’s death, binding the Gupta and Vakataka empires together and extending Gupta influence into the Deccan.

relationships.note: Daughter; her marriage into the Vakataka dynasty linked the Gupta and Vakataka empires.

journey.label: Rules the Vakataka realm as regent
journey.summary: Governs the Vakataka kingdom as regent for her young sons, strengthening Gupta ties to the Deccan.

name: Ramachandra
summary: Yadava ruler of Devagiri (Daulatabad) in the Deccan; forced to submit and pay tribute after Alauddin Khalji’s general’s raids, becoming one of the first major Deccan kingdoms to fall under Delhi Sultanate pressure.

relationships.note: Forced to submit and pay tribute to Delhi after Khalji invasions of Devagiri.

journey.label: Submits to Alauddin Khalji
journey.summary: Forced to accept tributary status to the Delhi Sultanate after Alauddin Khalji’s invasion of Devagiri.

name: Kharavela
summary: Powerful king of Kalinga whose military campaigns across eastern and southern India, and extensive public works, are recorded in his own Hathigumpha cave inscription — one of the most detailed royal autobiographies to survive from ancient India.

journey.label: Records his reign at Hathigumpha
journey.summary: Rules Kalinga from the capital near Sisupalgarh, commemorating his conquests and public works in the Hathigumpha inscription.

name: Gondophares
summary: Founded the Indo-Parthian Kingdom in the northwest, controlling territory from Afghanistan to the Indus; known from the Takht-i-Bahi inscription and coinage, and from later Christian tradition as the king the Apostle Thomas is said to have visited.

journey.label: Rules the Indo-Parthian Kingdom
journey.summary: Governs the Indo-Parthian Kingdom from the Taxila region, attested by his own coinage and inscriptions.

name: Maues
summary: First Indo-Scythian king to rule in the Indian subcontinent, establishing Saka power in Gandhara and the Punjab; known chiefly from his own coinage.

journey.label: Establishes Indo-Scythian rule
journey.summary: Rules the Gandhara-Punjab region as the first Indo-Scythian king, per his own coinage.

name: Prabhakaravardhana
role: King of the Pushyabhuti dynasty, father of Harsha
summary: King of Thanesar and father of Harsha and Rajyavardhana; expanded Pushyabhuti power before his death triggered the succession crisis that led to Harsha’s rise.

relationships.note: Father; his death triggered the succession crisis that brought Harsha to power.

journey.label: Rules the Pushyabhuti kingdom from Thanesar
journey.summary: Governs the Pushyabhuti kingdom from Thanesar before his death leads to a succession crisis.

name: Karikala
role: Most celebrated king of the early (Sangam-era) Chola kingdom
summary: Early Chola king celebrated in Sangam-era Tamil poetry for his military victories and for building the Kallanai (Grand Anicut) dam across the Kaveri river, still in use today.

journey.label: Rules the early Chola kingdom from Uraiyur
journey.summary: Governs the early Chola kingdom from Uraiyur and builds the Kallanai dam across the Kaveri.

name: Dutugemunu
summary: King of Anuradhapura who reunified Sri Lanka under his rule after defeating the Chola-descended king Elara; a central hero of the Mahavamsa chronicle and of Sri Lankan Buddhist national memory.

journey.label: Reunifies Sri Lanka
journey.summary: Defeats King Elara and reunifies the island under Anuradhapura rule, per the Mahavamsa chronicle.

name: Bhatarka
role: Founder of the Maitraka dynasty of Valabhi
summary: Former Gupta military governor of Saurashtra who, as central Gupta authority weakened, founded the independent Maitraka dynasty at Valabhi, which grew into a major center of Buddhist learning.

journey.label: Founds the Maitraka dynasty
journey.summary: Establishes independent Maitraka rule in Saurashtra from the capital Valabhi as Gupta central authority weakens.

name: Ishanavarman
role: King of the Maukhari dynasty of Kannauj
summary: Maukhari king who took the imperial title Maharajadhiraja after victories over the Hunas and neighboring kingdoms, establishing Kannauj as a major power in the Gangetic plain before the rise of Harsha’s allies there.

journey.label: Rules the Maukhari kingdom from Kannauj
journey.summary: Governs the Maukhari kingdom from Kannauj after victories that let him claim the imperial title Maharajadhiraja.

name: Anangpal II
role: Tomara Rajput king, founder of Lal Kot (Delhi)
summary: Tomara Rajput king traditionally credited with founding Lal Kot, the fortified citadel that became the nucleus of the city of Delhi, and with the Iron Pillar’s installation at its present site.

journey.label: Founds Lal Kot
journey.summary: Founds the fortified citadel of Lal Kot, the nucleus from which the city of Delhi grew.

name: Parakramabahu I
summary: Greatest king of Polonnaruwa, reunifying Sri Lanka under his rule and overseeing a massive expansion of irrigation works, including the Parakrama Samudra reservoir; his reign marks the island’s medieval political and architectural peak.

journey.label: Rules a reunified Sri Lanka from Polonnaruwa
journey.summary: Governs a reunified Sri Lanka from Polonnaruwa at the height of its medieval power.

name: Krishnaraja
role: Founder of the early Kalachuri dynasty
summary: Founded the early Kalachuri dynasty centered on Mahishmati in the Narmada valley; his family’s power is recorded in later Chalukya inscriptions, including the Aihole inscription.

journey.label: Founds the Kalachuri dynasty
journey.summary: Establishes Kalachuri rule in the Narmada valley from the region of Mahishmati.

name: Sripurusha
role: King of the Western Ganga dynasty
summary: Long-reigning Western Ganga king of Gangavadi (southern Karnataka) who took the title Prithvi-Konkani and held his own against both Pallava and Rashtrakuta pressure.

journey.label: Rules Gangavadi
journey.summary: Governs the Western Ganga kingdom of Gangavadi from the Kaveri valley region around Talakad.

name: Karna Vaghela
role: Last Hindu king of independent Gujarat
summary: Last king of the Vaghela dynasty of Gujarat; defeated by Alauddin Khalji’s invasion of 1304, ending independent Hindu rule in Gujarat and bringing it under the Delhi Sultanate.

relationships.note: Defeated by Alauddin Khalji’s 1304 invasion of Gujarat, ending the Vaghela dynasty.

journey.label: Defeated by Alauddin Khalji
journey.summary: Loses his kingdom to Alauddin Khalji’s invasion, ending the last independent Hindu dynasty of Gujarat.

name: Jalaluddin Ahsan Khan
role: Founder of the independent Madurai Sultanate
summary: Delhi-appointed governor of Madurai who declared independence from the Delhi Sultanate in 1335, founding the short-lived Madurai Sultanate, the southernmost Muslim kingdom in Indian history.

journey.label: Declares independence at Madurai
journey.summary: Breaks from Delhi Sultanate authority and founds the independent Madurai Sultanate.

name: Ekoji I
role: Founder of the Thanjavur Maratha kingdom
summary: Half-brother of Shivaji (son of Shahaji by his second wife Tukabai); carved out an independent Maratha kingdom at Thanjavur in the Tamil country in 1676, founding a dynasty that endured into the colonial era.

relationships.note: Son of Shahaji by his second wife Tukabai; half-brother of Shivaji.
Half-brother; the two founded separate Maratha kingdoms at Satara and Thanjavur.

journey.label: Founds the Thanjavur Maratha kingdom
journey.summary: Establishes an independent Maratha kingdom at Thanjavur in the Tamil country.

name: Nedunjeliyan
role: King of the early Pandya kingdom
summary: Early Pandya king celebrated in Sangam Tamil poetry for his victory at the battle of Talaiyalanganam over a confederacy of enemies, including the Chera and Chola kings.

journey.label: Wins the battle of Talaiyalanganam
journey.summary: Rules the early Pandya kingdom from Madurai after defeating a rival confederacy, celebrated in Sangam poetry.

name: Vimaladharmasuriya I
role: Founder of the Kingdom of Kandy as an independent power
summary: Established Kandy as an independent Sinhalese kingdom in the island’s interior, successfully resisting Portuguese expansion and bringing the sacred Tooth Relic of the Buddha to Kandy, cementing its religious significance.

journey.label: Establishes Kandy as an independent kingdom
journey.summary: Makes Kandy the capital of an independent Sinhalese kingdom resisting Portuguese expansion.

name: Malik Raja Faruqi
role: Founder of the Faruqi dynasty of Khandesh
summary: Delhi Sultanate noble who, as central authority weakened under Firuz Shah Tughlaq’s successors, established the independent Faruqi dynasty in Khandesh, controlling the strategic corridor between Malwa and the Deccan.

journey.label: Founds the Faruqi dynasty of Khandesh
journey.summary: Establishes independent Faruqi rule over Khandesh, controlling the Malwa-Deccan corridor.

name: Shuja-ud-Daula
summary: Nawab of Awadh who joined the Mughal emperor and the Nawab of Bengal against the British East India Company; defeated at the Battle of Buxar in 1764, after which Awadh fell increasingly under British influence.

journey.label: Defeated at the Battle of Buxar
journey.summary: Rules Awadh from Lucknow; defeated alongside Mughal and Bengal allies at Buxar, opening Awadh to growing British control.

name: Dost Mohammad Khan
summary: Afghan mercenary in Mughal service who, as central authority weakened after Aurangzeb’s death, carved out and founded the princely state of Bhopal.

journey.label: Founds Bhopal State
journey.summary: Establishes an independent principality at Bhopal from his Mughal military holdings.

name: Mahabat Khanji II
summary: Last ruling Nawab of Junagadh; initially acceded to Pakistan at independence in 1947, a decision reversed after popular unrest and Indian pressure, and Junagadh joined India in 1948.

journey.label: Accedes Junagadh to Pakistan, then reversed
journey.summary: Announces accession to Pakistan; the decision is overturned after unrest, and Junagadh joins India in 1948.

name: Sadeq Mohammad Khan V
summary: Last ruling Nawab of Bahawalpur, a major princely state in the Punjab; acceded the state to Pakistan in 1947 rather than to India, a decisive choice given Bahawalpur’s location.

journey.label: Accedes Bahawalpur to Pakistan
journey.summary: Rules Bahawalpur State and accedes it to the new state of Pakistan at independence.

name: Ala Singh
role: Founder of the Patiala princely state
summary: Sikh Jat chief who founded the Phulkian state of Patiala, consolidating territory in the Malwa region of the Punjab as Mughal authority collapsed.

journey.label: Founds Patiala State
journey.summary: Establishes the city and princely state of Patiala as the seat of the Phulkian dynasty.

name: Rao Madho Singh
role: Founder of the Hada Chauhan state of Kota
summary: Younger son of the Bundi Rao, granted the territory of Kota by Mughal emperor Jahangir as a separate fief in 1631, founding the princely state of Kota.

journey.label: Founds Kota State
journey.summary: Receives Kota as a separate Mughal-granted fief, founding the Hada Chauhan state of Kota.

name: Vyaghra Deva
role: Founder of the Baghel dynasty of Rewa
summary: Traditional founder of the Baghel Rajput line that later established the princely state of Rewa in the Vindhya region, named for the clan’s tiger (vyaghra) emblem.

journey.label: Founds the Baghel line at Rewa
journey.summary: Establishes the Baghel Rajput line in the Vindhya region, from which the state of Rewa later grew.

name: Mir Naseer Khan I
summary: Most powerful Khan of Kalat, consolidating Baloch tribal confederacies under centralized rule and successfully resisting incursions from Afghanistan and Persia during his long reign.

journey.label: Consolidates the Khanate of Kalat
journey.summary: Centralizes Baloch tribal rule under the Khanate of Kalat, resisting external incursions.

name: Biswa Singha
role: Founder of the Koch Bihar dynasty
summary: Founded the Koch dynasty of Koch Bihar in the northeastern frontier of Bengal and Assam, unifying the Koch tribal territories into a centralized kingdom.

journey.label: Founds the Koch kingdom
journey.summary: Unifies Koch tribal territories into the centralized kingdom of Koch Bihar.

name: Rao Khengarji I
role: Founder of the princely state of Kutch
summary: Jadeja Rajput chief who founded the city of Bhuj and established Kutch as a unified princely state in Gujarat’s western peninsula.

journey.label: Founds Bhuj and the state of Kutch
journey.summary: Establishes Bhuj as his capital and unifies Kutch as a princely state.

name: Rao Bika
summary: Rathore prince, younger son of Rao Jodha of Marwar, who struck out on his own to found the city and princely state of Bikaner in 1488.

relationships.note: Father; Rao Bika left Marwar to found his own state at Bikaner.

journey.label: Founds Bikaner
journey.summary: Founds the city and state of Bikaner after leaving his father’s court at Marwar.

name: Pamheiba
summary: Most powerful king of Manipur, expanding its territory and launching repeated raids into neighboring Burmese-controlled territory; converted the kingdom to Vaishnavism, reshaping Manipuri culture and religion.

journey.label: Rules Manipur at its height
journey.summary: Governs Manipur from Imphal, expanding its territory and converting the kingdom to Vaishnavism.

name: Phuntsog Namgyal
role: Founder of the Kingdom of Sikkim
summary: Consecrated as the first Chogyal (king) of Sikkim in 1642, founding the Namgyal dynasty that ruled Sikkim until its merger with India in 1975.

journey.label: Consecrated first Chogyal of Sikkim
journey.summary: Becomes the first Chogyal of Sikkim, founding the Namgyal dynasty.

name: Man Singh Tomar
summary: Tomar king of Gwalior renowned for building the Man Mandir palace within Gwalior Fort and for his patronage of music, including the Dhrupad style of Hindustani classical singing.

journey.label: Builds Man Mandir at Gwalior Fort
journey.summary: Rules Gwalior as a Tomar king, building the Man Mandir palace and patronizing Dhrupad music.

name: Jiva Mahala
summary: One of Shivaji's personal bodyguards at the parley with Afzal Khan on Pratapgad in 1659; cut off the hand of Khan's bodyguard Sayyed Banda as he moved to strike Shivaji, saving his life at the critical moment.

relationships.note: Bodyguard; saved his life at the Pratapgad parley by disabling Sayyed Banda.
Cut off Sayyed Banda's hand as he attacked Shivaji at the Pratapgad parley.

journey.label: Saves Shivaji at the Pratapgad parley
journey.summary: Disables Afzal Khan's bodyguard Sayyed Banda as he lunges at Shivaji, preventing the attack.

name: Sayyed Banda
summary: Afzal Khan's personal bodyguard; struck at Shivaji with a sword during the Pratapgad parley after Khan's own attack failed, but was disabled by Jiva Mahala before he could land a fatal blow.

relationships.note: Personal bodyguard who attacked Shivaji during the Pratapgad parley.
Disabled by Jiva Mahala as he attacked Shivaji at Pratapgad.

journey.label: Attacks Shivaji at the Pratapgad parley
journey.summary: Strikes at Shivaji during the parley but is disabled before the blow lands.

name: Sambhaji Kavji Kondhalkar
summary: Maratha warrior present at the Pratapgad parley in 1659; by most accounts beheaded Afzal Khan's body after Shivaji mortally wounded him, and carried the head back to the Maratha camp.

relationships.note: Present at the Pratapgad parley; beheaded Afzal Khan after Shivaji struck him down.

journey.label: Beheads Afzal Khan
journey.summary: Beheads Afzal Khan's body after the parley and carries the head back to the Maratha camp.

name: Siddi Jauhar
summary: Abyssinian-origin Bijapur general sent to besiege Shivaji at the fort of Panhala in 1660; the prolonged siege forced Shivaji’s night escape to Vishalgad, covered by Baji Prabhu Deshpande’s last stand at Pavan Khind.

relationships.note: Besieged him at Panhala in 1660, forcing his escape to Vishalgad.
His siege of Panhala set up the pursuit that Baji Prabhu Deshpande's stand at Pavan Khind blocked.

journey.label: Besieges Shivaji at Panhala
journey.summary: Lays siege to Panhala fort, forcing Shivaji's night escape toward Vishalgad.

name: Baji Pasalkar
summary: One of Shivaji’s earliest and most trusted commanders in the Pune region during his rise; died fighting the Mores of Jawli during Shivaji’s campaign to subdue that independent chiefdom.

relationships.note: Early trusted commander; died fighting the Mores of Jawli in his service.

journey.label: Dies fighting the Mores of Jawli
journey.summary: Killed in the fighting that brought the independent chiefdom of Jawli under Shivaji's control.

name: Bahirji Naik Jadhav
summary: Credited in Maratha tradition with building and running Shivaji's intelligence network, whose timely information on troop movements, routes, and enemy plans — including ahead of the Pratapgad meeting with Afzal Khan — underpinned many of his campaigns.

relationships.note: Ran his intelligence network, feeding him information before major campaigns including Pratapgad.

journey.label: Feeds intelligence ahead of the Afzal Khan meeting
journey.summary: Supplies intelligence on Afzal Khan's movements and intentions ahead of the Pratapgad parley.

name: Balaji Avji Chitnis
summary: Served as Shivaji's chief secretary (Chitnis), drafting his official correspondence and records; continued in the same role under Sambhaji and was executed by the Mughals alongside him in 1689.

relationships.note: Chief secretary (Chitnis), drafting his official correspondence.
Continued as Chitnis under Sambhaji and was executed alongside him by the Mughals in 1689.

journey.label: Serves as Chitnis at the Raigad court
journey.summary: Drafts and manages official correspondence as Shivaji's chief secretary.

name: Raghunath Narayan Hanmante
role: Diplomat and administrator in Shivaji's southern campaign
summary: Brahmin administrator who negotiated on Shivaji's behalf with the Qutb Shahi court of Golconda and helped organize the 1677 Karnatak expedition, securing both an alliance and financial backing for the southern campaign.

relationships.note: Negotiated the Golconda alliance and helped organize the 1677 Karnatak campaign.

journey.label: Negotiates the Golconda alliance
journey.summary: Helps arrange the alliance with the Qutb Shahi court that backed Shivaji's 1677 Karnatak expedition.

name: Ramchandra Pant Nilkanth Amatya
role: Amatya (finance minister) among the Ashta Pradhan
summary: Held the office of Amatya (finance and revenue minister), one of the eight ministers (Ashta Pradhan) of Shivaji's formal council of state established after his 1674 coronation.

relationships.note: Amatya (finance minister) in his Ashta Pradhan council of state.

journey.label: Appointed Amatya in the Ashta Pradhan
journey.summary: Takes office as Amatya in the formal council of eight ministers established at the coronation.

name: Kartalab Khan
summary: Mughal commander sent to intercept Shivaji during his return march after the 1660 Panhala campaign; ambushed and routed in the narrow Umberkhind pass in 1661, one of Shivaji’s most effective uses of terrain against a larger force.

relationships.note: Ambushed and defeated by Shivaji in the Umberkhind pass, 1661.

journey.label: Ambushed at Umberkhind
journey.summary: Routed in the narrow Umberkhind pass after Shivaji's forces attack from the surrounding heights.

name: Ali Adil Shah II
summary: Sultan of Bijapur during Shivaji’s rise; sent Afzal Khan against him in 1659 and continued to contest Maratha expansion from the weakening Bijapur Sultanate for the rest of his reign.

relationships.note: Sent Afzal Khan against him in 1659, a mission that ended in Khan's death.
Sent him against Shivaji in 1659.

journey.label: Sends Afzal Khan against Shivaji
journey.summary: Dispatches his general Afzal Khan to suppress the rising power of Shivaji.

name: Fazl Khan
summary: Son of Afzal Khan; took command of the Bijapur force after his father's death at Pratapgad in 1659, but was defeated and driven from the field by Shivaji's pursuing Marathas soon after.

relationships.note: Son; took command of his father's Bijapur force after his death at Pratapgad.
Defeated and driven from the field after taking command following his father Afzal Khan's death.

journey.label: Defeated after taking his father's command
journey.summary: Takes command of the routed Bijapur force after his father's death and is driven from the field.

name: Putalabai
summary: One of Shivaji's wives; performed sati on his funeral pyre at Raigad after his death in 1680, as recorded in contemporary Maratha chronicles.

relationships.note: Wife; performed sati on his funeral pyre at Raigad in 1680.

journey.label: Performs sati on Shivaji's pyre
journey.summary: Dies by sati on Shivaji's funeral pyre at Raigad.

name: Rustam Zaman
summary: Bijapur general defeated by Shivaji's forces near Kolhapur in December 1659, shortly after the killing of Afzal Khan, in one of the Marathas' first open-field victories over a regular Bijapur army.

relationships.note: Defeated near Kolhapur in December 1659.

journey.label: Defeated near Kolhapur
journey.summary: Defeated in open-field battle near Kolhapur shortly after Afzal Khan's death.

name: Hiroji Farzand
role: Maratha officer who impersonated Shivaji during the Agra escape
summary: A Maratha officer closely resembling Shivaji; after the escape from Mughal custody at Agra in 1666, he continued to occupy Shivaji's palanquin and play his part in public for several days, buying time for the real Shivaji to get clear of Mughal territory.

relationships.note: Impersonated him in his palanquin for days after the 1666 Agra escape, covering his retreat.

journey.label: Impersonates Shivaji after the Agra escape
journey.summary: Occupies Shivaji's palanquin and plays his part in public after the escape, covering his retreat north.

name: Madari Mehtar
role: Barber who helped plan Shivaji's escape from Agra
summary: A barber in Shivaji's retinue at Agra who helped plan and carry out his 1666 escape from Mughal house-arrest, reputedly taking his place as guard-decoy and later being rewarded with a village grant.

relationships.note: Helped plan and carry out his 1666 escape from Mughal custody at Agra.

journey.label: Helps plan the escape from Agra
journey.summary: Assists in planning and carrying out Shivaji's escape from Mughal custody.

name: Niraji Raoji Pant
role: Nyayadhish (chief justice) among the Ashta Pradhan
summary: Held the office of Nyayadhish (chief justice), one of the eight ministers of Shivaji's Ashta Pradhan council of state formed after his 1674 coronation, responsible for the administration of justice.

relationships.note: Nyayadhish (chief justice) in his Ashta Pradhan council of state.

journey.label: Appointed Nyayadhish in the Ashta Pradhan
journey.summary: Takes office as Nyayadhish, overseeing the administration of justice in the new kingdom.

name: Diler Khan
summary: Afghan Mughal general who joined Jai Singh I's 1665 siege of Purandar that forced Shivaji's treaty, and went on to lead repeated Mughal campaigns against the Marathas and Bijapur in the Deccan for the next two decades.

relationships.note: Joined Jai Singh I's 1665 siege of Purandar.
Took part in the 1665 Purandar siege that forced the treaty ceding 23 forts.

journey.label: Joins the siege of Purandar
journey.summary: Takes part in Jai Singh I's siege of Purandar, which forced Shivaji's 1665 treaty with the Mughals.

name: Muhammad Muazzam
role: Aurangzeb's son, Mughal viceroy of the Deccan
summary: Aurangzeb's second son, sent to the Deccan as viceroy where he dealt directly with Maratha affairs after Shivaji's death, including negotiations and conflicts with Sambhaji; later succeeded his father as Emperor Bahadur Shah I in 1707.

relationships.note: Son; later succeeded him as Emperor Bahadur Shah I.
As Mughal viceroy of the Deccan, dealt directly with Sambhaji's Maratha kingdom.

journey.label: Serves as Mughal viceroy of the Deccan
journey.summary: Governs the Deccan on his father's behalf, overseeing Mughal dealings with Sambhaji's Maratha kingdom.

name: Sakhubai
summary: Shivaji's eldest daughter, married to Mahadji Nimbalkar as part of a marriage alliance binding a Maratha deshmukh family to the new Bhonsle state.

relationships.note: Father; married her to Mahadji Nimbalkar as a political alliance.

journey.label: Marriage alliance with the Nimbalkar family
journey.summary: Married to Mahadji Nimbalkar, binding the Nimbalkar deshmukh family to the Bhonsle state.

name: Ranubai
summary: Shivaji's daughter, married into the Jadhav family — the same clan as his maternal grandfather Lakhoji Jadhavrao — reinforcing ties between the Bhonsle state and allied Maratha deshmukh houses.

relationships.note: Father; married her into the Jadhav family.

journey.label: Marriage alliance with the Jadhav family
journey.summary: Married into the Jadhav family, reinforcing ties to allied Maratha deshmukh houses.

name: Abul Fazl
summary: Akbar's close adviser and grand vizier, and author of the Akbarnama, the official chronicle of Akbar's reign, and the Ain-i-Akbari, a detailed administrative gazetteer; one of the most important Mughal intellectuals and one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court.

relationships.note: Grand vizier and author of the Akbarnama, the official chronicle of his reign.

journey.label: Writes the Akbarnama
journey.summary: Compiles the Akbarnama, the official chronicle of Akbar's reign, at the Mughal court.

name: Raja Todar Mal
summary: Served as Akbar's finance minister and designed the Mughal Empire's systematic land revenue settlement (the zabt system), standardizing assessment and collection across the empire; one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court.

relationships.note: Finance minister who designed the empire's systematic land revenue settlement.

journey.label: Designs the Mughal revenue settlement
journey.summary: Implements a standardized land revenue assessment system across the Mughal Empire.

name: Tansen
summary: Legendary Hindustani classical musician at Akbar's court, credited with composing numerous ragas and founding a lineage of musicians; one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court.

relationships.note: Court musician celebrated as one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of his court.

journey.label: Joins Akbar's court
journey.summary: Becomes the leading musician at Akbar's court, composing ragas still performed in Hindustani classical music.

name: Birbal
summary: Close courtier and adviser to Akbar, celebrated in later folklore for his wit; one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court. Killed in 1586 while leading an army against the Yusufzai tribes in the northwest frontier, one of the few major military defeats of Akbar's reign.

relationships.note: Close courtier; killed in 1586 leading an army against the Yusufzai tribes.

journey.label: Killed campaigning against the Yusufzai
journey.summary: Dies leading a Mughal force against the Yusufzai tribes in the Khyber region, a rare major defeat for Akbar's armies.

name: Abdul Rahim
role: Mughal general, poet, and one of Akbar's Navratnas
summary: Son of Bairam Khan, raised at Akbar's court after his father's fall from power; became one of Akbar's leading generals and the title-holder Khan-i-Khanan, and is remembered today chiefly as a major Hindi/Braj Bhasha poet, writing under the pen name Rahim.

relationships.note: Son; raised at Akbar's court after his father's fall from power.
Leading general and poet at his court, holding the title Khan-i-Khanan.

journey.label: Rises as a leading Mughal general and poet
journey.summary: Serves Akbar as a leading general, holding the title Khan-i-Khanan, while composing celebrated Braj Bhasha poetry.

name: Hamida Banu Begum
summary: Wife of Humayun and mother of Akbar; accompanied Humayun through his years of exile in Persia and lived to see her son's long reign, dying at Agra in 1604.

relationships.note: Wife; accompanied him through his years of exile in Persia.
Mother; lived to see most of his long reign.

journey.label: Gives birth to Akbar during Humayun’s exile
journey.summary: Gives birth to Akbar at Umerkot while accompanying Humayun during his years of exile.

name: Maham Anga
role: Akbar's foster mother and early political power-broker
summary: Akbar's wet-nurse and foster mother, whose household became the dominant political faction at court during his minority after Bairam Khan's fall; her influence ended after her son Adham Khan was executed on Akbar's orders in 1562.

relationships.note: Foster mother and dominant court power-broker during his minority.
Son; her influence collapsed after his execution on Akbar’s orders in 1562.

journey.label: Dominates the court during Akbar’s minority
journey.summary: Leads the dominant court faction during Akbar's minority after Bairam Khan's removal.

name: Adham Khan
summary: Son of Akbar's foster mother Maham Anga; a Mughal general who, after murdering a rival minister at court, was thrown from the ramparts of Agra Fort on Akbar's personal order in 1562, ending his mother's dominance over the court.

relationships.note: Mother; her influence collapsed after his execution.
Executed on his personal order in 1562 after murdering a rival minister.

journey.label: Executed on Akbar’s order
journey.summary: Thrown from the ramparts of Agra Fort on Akbar's order after murdering a rival court minister.
